definition_zh: 国际贸易；跨越国界的货物与服务交换
definition_en: the exchange of goods and services across national borders
core_image: 港口堆着成排集装箱，吊机把箱子从船上移到岸上，报关单在窗口逐个盖章
scene: 港口堆着成排集装箱，吊机把箱子从一艘船移到岸上，报关单在窗口盖章。 International trade grew faster than output for most of the last century.
sceneCN: 这里这个词组指「跨国界的货物交换」（第 1 个义项：货物跨境买卖）；句意为在上个世纪的大部分时间里，国际贸易的增长快于产出。图中可辨识物件：集装箱、吊机、货船、报关窗口的印章。

senses.title: Cross-border exchange of goods
senses.definition: the buying and selling of physical goods between countries
senses.definitionCN: 国家之间对实物货物的买进与卖出
senses.example: International trade in grain depends on port capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 谷物的国际贸易取决于港口吞吐能力。
senses.why: Two words say it plainly: trade that crosses between nations.
senses.whyCN: 两个词把意思说得很直白：在国家之间越过的买卖。

senses.title: Trade in services across borders
senses.definition: the sale of transport, finance, tourism or advice between countries
senses.definitionCN: 国家之间出售运输、金融、旅游或咨询
senses.example: International trade in services now exceeds trade in many goods.
senses.exampleCN: 服务贸易如今超过了许多货物的贸易。
senses.why: A service can be exported without a crate, and the phrase still applies.
senses.whyCN: 服务不需要木箱也能出口，而这个短语仍然适用。

senses.title: The rules and institutions of trade
senses.definition: the laws, treaties and bodies that govern exchange between countries
senses.definitionCN: 管理国家间交换的法律、条约与机构
senses.example: International trade law governs the dispute over the shipment.
senses.exampleCN: 国际贸易法管辖这起货物运输纠纷。
senses.why: Once trade crosses borders, it needs rules, and the phrase names the whole regime.
senses.whyCN: 一旦贸易越过国界，就需要规则，这个短语于是指整套制度。

senses.title: The balance of exports and imports
senses.definition: the difference between what a country sells abroad and what it buys
senses.definitionCN: 一国卖到国外与从国外买入之间的差额
senses.example: The trade balance turned negative after energy prices rose.
senses.exampleCN: 能源价格上涨之后，贸易差额转为逆差。
senses.why: Two flows in opposite directions invite a subtraction, and the balance is that result.
senses.whyCN: 两股方向相反的流自然引出减法，差额就是那个结果。

senses.title: Agreements that open or close markets
senses.titleCN: 打开或关闭市场的协定
senses.definition: treaties that lower barriers or set quotas between signatory countries
senses.definitionCN: 在签署国之间降低壁垒或设定配额的条约
senses.example: The new agreement reshaped international trade in machinery.
senses.exampleCN: 新协定重塑了机械领域的国际贸易。
senses.why: Governments bargain over access, and the agreement becomes part of what the phrase covers.
senses.whyCN: 各国政府为市场准入而谈判，协定就成了这个短语所涵盖的一部分。

senses.title: The theory of why countries exchange
senses.titleCN: 解释各国为何交换的理论
senses.definition: the economic study of specialization and comparative advantage between nations
senses.definitionCN: 研究国家之间专业化与比较优势的经济学问
senses.example: The course begins with the theory of international trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从国际贸易理论讲起。
senses.why: The phenomenon becomes an object of study, and the phrase names the field.
senses.whyCN: 这一现象成为研究对象，这个短语就成了学科名。

senses.title: Recorded flows in statistics
senses.definition: the measured value of goods and services exchanged, published as data
senses.definitionCN: 被测量并公布为数据的货物与服务交换值
senses.example: International trade statistics are revised every quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 国际贸易统计数据每季度修订一次。
senses.why: Customs records turn millions of shipments into aggregate flows.
senses.whyCN: 海关记录把数以百万计的货运变成汇总的流动。

senses.title: Exchange of ideas and culture
senses.definition: the movement of knowledge, styles and people across borders, described as trade
senses.definitionCN: 知识、风格与人的跨境流动，被以「贸易」来描述
senses.example: Historians speak of an international trade in ideas along the caravan roads.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家谈到商队道路上思想的国家间交流。
senses.why: The phrase can be borrowed for anything that travels and is exchanged.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可被借去指任何会旅行并被交换的东西。

intro.en: The phrase joins international, coined in the eighteenth century from Latin inter between and natio birth, with trade, a Germanic word for a course of life that became commerce.
intro.cn: 这个短语把 international 与 trade 组合起来。international 是十八世纪用拉丁语 inter「之间」与 natio「出生」造出的词；trade 是日耳曼语词，本指生活方式，后转为商业。

items.en: Natio meant a birth or a people born together, from nasci, to be born.
items.cn: natio 意为「出生、同源而生的一群人」，来自 nasci「出生」。

items.en: Inter meant between or among, and it remains the first element of many modern compounds.
items.cn: inter 意为「在……之间」，至今仍是许多现代复合词的第一部分。

items.en: The adjective was coined in the late eighteenth century to mean between nations, and it spread with the growth of treaties and trade.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十八世纪后期被造出，意为「国家之间的」，随条约与贸易的发展而普及。

items.en: Trade came into English meaning a track or a way of life, and later narrowed to buying and selling.
items.cn: trade 进入英语时指路径或生活方式，后来收窄为买进卖出。

items.en: The two words joined once goods began to be counted across borders rather than only at local markets.
items.cn: 当货物开始被按跨境而非仅按本地市场统计时，这两个词走到了一起。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase came to name a system of rules, statistics and institutions, not only the shipments themselves.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个短语指一套规则、统计与机构，而不只是货运本身。

note.en: The first group holds the parts of the phrase and one prefix look-alike; the second holds other names for trade between countries.
note.cn: 第一组是短语的组成部分与一个前缀形近词；第二组是国家间贸易的其他叫法。

entries.definition: Between nations; it can describe law, sport or trade, and does not by itself mean commerce.
entries.definitionCN: 国家之间的；可修饰法律、体育或贸易，本身并不指商业。

entries.definition: A people or a state; it is the unit across which the trade moves.
entries.definitionCN: 一个民族或国家；它正是贸易所跨过的单位。

entries.definition: Buying and selling in general; the longer phrase only adds the crossing of borders.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指买进卖出；较长的短语只是加上了「跨越国界」。

entries.definition: Inside a country or an organization, from intra- within; it is the opposite of international in trade talk.
entries.definitionCN: 在一国或一个组织之内，来自 intra-「在内」；在贸易话题中正是国际的反面。

entries.definition: A single country's trade with others; the phrase takes the viewpoint of one state, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 某一国与其他国家的贸易；它取一国的视角，而非整个体系。

entries.definition: Trade considered as one worldwide network rather than as relations between nations.
entries.definitionCN: 把贸易看作一个全球网络，而非国家之间的关系。

entries.definition: Trade on a large scale; it may be internal as well as international.
entries.definitionCN: 大规模贸易；既可以是国际的，也可以是一国之内的。

entries.definition: The half of the exchange that sells abroad; the full phrase covers both directions.
entries.definitionCN: 交换中向外出售的那一半；完整短语涵盖两个方向。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real parts, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: International plus trade: buying and selling that crosses a border.
normal.cn: 「国家之间的」加「买卖」：越过边界的买进卖出。

normal.en: The parts are nation, inter- and trade, each with its own history.
normal.cn: 组成部分是「国家」「之间」与「买卖」，各有一段自己的历史。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark law, services and statistics: international trade law, trade in services, trade statistics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律、服务与统计：国际贸易法、服务贸易、贸易统计。

normal.en: Keep international and internal apart: one crosses out, one stays in.
normal.cn: 把「国际」与「内部」分开：一个跨出去，一个留在里面。

normal.en: A container crane lifting a box from ship to shore is the visible unit of the whole system.
normal.cn: 吊机把集装箱从船移到岸，就是整个体系可见的单位。

abstract.en: Picture two countries as two rooms with a door that only opens outward.
abstract.cn: 想象两个国家像两个房间，中间一扇门只朝外开。

abstract.en: Picture a map where borders are drawn as thin lines that goods must step over.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，边界被画成货物必须跨过的细线。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger with two columns, one for what leaves and one for what arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿有两栏，一栏记出去的，一栏记进来的。

examples.en: International trade slowed when the shipping lanes closed.
examples.cn: 航道关闭时，国际贸易放缓。

examples.en: The course covers international trade and its legal framework.
examples.cn: 这门课讲授国际贸易及其法律框架。

examples.en: Services now make up a larger share of international trade.
examples.cn: 服务现在占国际贸易的更大比重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「国家之间（international）的买卖（trade）」——货物与服务跨越国界的交换 → 国际贸易

root: international 由拉丁语 inter「之间」与 natio「出生、族群」构成，十八世纪后期造出；trade 来自日耳曼语，本指路径与生活方式，后指买卖。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one flow across a border: goods, services, the rules, the balance, the agreements, the theory, the statistics and finally ideas carried along the same roads.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一股跨境流动展开：货物、服务、规则、差额、协定、理论、统计，最后是沿着同一条路走的思想。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crane lifting a container from a ship while a customs officer stamps a form.
core.cn: 核心意象：吊机把集装箱从船上吊起，海关关员同时在报关单上盖章。

branches.en: WHAT MOVES: a crate and a service are two forms of the same export.
branches.cn: 移动的东西：木箱与服务是同一种出口的两种形态。

branches.en: THE RULES: law and agreements are the border turned into text.
branches.cn: 规则：法律与协定就是把边界写成了文字。

branches.en: THE BALANCE: two opposite flows invite a subtraction.
branches.cn: 差额：两股相反的流自然引出减法。

branches.en: THE THEORY: the flow becomes an object of study.
branches.cn: 理论：这股流动成为研究对象。

branches.en: COUNTED AND BORROWED: statistics turn shipments into data, and the phrase stretches to ideas.
branches.cn: 被计数与被借用：统计把货运变成数据，短语又被拉到思想上。

intro.en: The phrase is a Latin-built adjective of betweenness plus a Germanic noun of practice, so it reads as dealing that goes between nations.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个用拉丁语成分构成的「之间」形容词加一个日耳曼语表示行当的名词组成，读作「在国家之间进行的买卖」。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter and natio build international; trade itself is Germanic and brings no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 与 natio 构成 international；trade 本身属日耳曼语，不带来拉丁词根。

items.example: The prefix places the action between two parties.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作放在两方之间。

items.example: The noun gives the word its unit of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「归属单位」这一层。

items.example: The rule applies to international shipments.
items.exampleCN: 这条规则适用于国际货运。

items.example: Trade moved along the river for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 几百年来贸易沿着这条河进行。

items.example: International trade needs ports and paperwork.
items.exampleCN: 国际贸易需要港口与文书。

items.example: The exporter bears the freight cost.
items.exampleCN: 出口商承担运费。

items.example: The importer clears the goods at customs.
items.exampleCN: 进口商在海关清关。

items.example: The trade balance compares two flows.
items.exampleCN: 贸易差额比较两股流动。

items.example: Statistics record what crosses the border.
items.exampleCN: 统计记录越过边界的东西。

definition_zh: 呼吸的；呼吸系统的；呼吸器官的
definition_en: relating to breathing or to the organs and passages used for breathing
core_image: 一条从鼻腔到肺泡的通路，空气沿路进出
scene: 这里指「呼吸的」。 Smoking damages the respiratory tract from the throat to the alveoli.
sceneCN: 这里 respiratory 指「呼吸道的」（第 4 个义项：空气所经的鼻腔、咽、气管与支气管）；句意：吸烟损害从咽喉到肺泡的呼吸道。图中可辨识物件：鼻腔、气管、支气管树、肺泡。

pos.zh: 呼吸的；呼吸系统的；呼吸器官的

senses.title: Relating to breathing
senses.titleCN: 呼吸的：与呼吸动作有关
senses.definition: connected with the act of breathing
senses.definitionCN: 与呼吸动作有关的
senses.example: Respiratory effort increases during exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 运动时呼吸做功增加。
senses.why: Latin respiratorius is a functional adjective, so the word begins as 'serving breathing'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 respiratorius 是功能形容词，因此这个词起初意为「服务于呼吸的」。

senses.title: Of the respiratory system
senses.titleCN: 呼吸系统的：鼻腔到肺的整套结构
senses.definition: belonging to the whole system of passages and organs used in breathing
senses.definitionCN: 属于呼吸所用的整套通道与器官
senses.example: The respiratory system includes the nose, trachea and lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸系统包括鼻、气管与肺。
senses.why: Anatomy grouped the passages into one system and needed a single adjective for it.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把这些通道归为一个系统，需要单一形容词来指称。

senses.title: Of respiratory organs
senses.titleCN: 呼吸器官的：肺、鳃、气囊等
senses.definition: describes the organs that carry out gas exchange, such as lungs, gills or air sacs
senses.definitionCN: 形容执行气体交换的器官，如肺、鳃或气囊
senses.example: Bird respiratory organs include air sacs as well as lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟的呼吸器官除肺之外还包括气囊。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the organ itself, not only to the function.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词附着于器官本身，而不只是功能。

senses.title: Of the respiratory tract
senses.titleCN: 呼吸道的：空气经过的管道
senses.definition: describes the tube from nose and mouth down to the alveoli
senses.definitionCN: 形容从口鼻向下直到肺泡的管道
senses.example: Smoking damages the respiratory tract from the throat to the alveoli.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟损害从咽喉到肺泡的呼吸道。
senses.why: Clinical writing needed a word for the route rather than for the organ at its end.
senses.whyCN: 临床写作需要指称这条路径，而非其末端的器官。

senses.title: Respiratory disease
senses.titleCN: 呼吸系统疾病：影响通气或交换的病症
senses.definition: describes illness of the airways or lungs, such as asthma or pneumonia
senses.definitionCN: 形容气道或肺部的疾病，如哮喘或肺炎
senses.example: Respiratory disease is a leading cause of hospital admission.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸系统疾病是入院的主要原因之一。
senses.why: Clinical medicine groups illnesses of the airways and lungs under one adjective because they share the same passages and the same symptoms.
senses.whyCN: 临床医学把气道与肺的疾病归在同一个形容词下，因为它们共用同一条通道，也共用同一组症状。

senses.title: Respiratory failure
senses.titleCN: 呼吸衰竭：气体交换不足以维持血液氧合
senses.definition: a condition in which the lungs cannot keep blood oxygen or carbon dioxide within safe limits
senses.definitionCN: 肺无法把血氧或二氧化碳维持在安全范围内的状态
senses.example: Respiratory failure required mechanical ventilation.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸衰竭需要使用机械通气。
senses.why: Failure names the point where gas exchange can no longer keep blood chemistry safe, so the adjective marks the breakdown of the organ itself.
senses.whyCN: 衰竭指的是气体交换已无法维持血液化学安全的那一点，因此这个形容词标记的是器官本身的崩溃。

senses.title: Respiratory rate
senses.titleCN: 呼吸频率：每分钟呼吸次数
senses.definition: the number of breaths taken per minute, a standard vital sign
senses.definitionCN: 每分钟呼吸的次数，是标准的生命体征
senses.example: The nurse recorded a respiratory rate of twenty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 护士记录呼吸频率为每分钟二十二次。
senses.why: Counting breaths per minute turns the adjective into a measurable number, the way heart rate counts beats.
senses.whyCN: 把每分钟的呼吸次数数出来，就把这个形容词变成一个可测量的数字，正如心率数的是心跳。

senses.title: Respiratory acidosis
senses.titleCN: 呼吸性酸中毒：通气不足导致二氧化碳蓄积
senses.definition: a blood chemistry disturbance caused by inadequate breathing, which retains carbon dioxide
senses.definitionCN: 因通气不足、二氧化碳滞留而引起的血液化学紊乱
senses.example: Respiratory acidosis showed up as a falling blood pH.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸性酸中毒表现为血液 pH 下降。
senses.why: Acidosis names the chemical result of retained carbon dioxide, so the adjective points to breathing as the cause rather than the effect.
senses.whyCN: 酸中毒命名的是二氧化碳滞留的化学结果，因此这个形容词指向的是作为原因的呼吸，而非结果。

intro.en: Respiratory is Latin respiratorius, formed on respiratio 'breathing', from respirare. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: respiratory 是拉丁 respiratorius，由 respiratio「呼吸」构成，而 respiratio 出自 respirare。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare 'to breathe, to blow' underlies a large family: spiritus, inspirare, expirare, suspirare and respirare.
items.cn: spirare「呼吸、吹」是大家族的基础：spiritus、inspirare、expirare、suspirare、respirare。

items.en: Respirare meant 'to breathe again, to recover breath'. Its action noun respiratio named breathing in general.
items.cn: respirare 意为「再次呼吸、缓过气来」，其动作名词 respiratio 泛指呼吸。

items.en: Respiratorius was a functional adjective meaning 'serving breathing'. It appears in later medical Latin rather than in classical prose.
items.cn: respiratorius 是功能形容词，意为「服务于呼吸的」，见于后世医学拉丁，而非古典散文。

items.en: English respiratory enters in the seventeenth century, first in medical descriptions of the lungs and their passages.
items.cn: 英语 respiratory 于 17 世纪进入，最早见于对肺及其通道的医学描述。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century medicine built fixed phrases such as respiratory system, respiratory tract, respiratory failure and respiratory rate.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的医学构造了 respiratory system、respiratory tract、respiratory failure、respiratory rate 等固定短语。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper root behind spirare is reconstructed, not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：英语最早书证年代存疑；spirare 背后的更深词根属重构形式，并无记录。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for the organs and functions of breathing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是「呼吸器官与功能」的近义词。

entries.definition: The process or one breath; the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或一次呼吸；形容词描述属于它的事物。

entries.definition: To breathe; it names the action, while respiratory describes a structure or function.
entries.definitionCN: 呼吸；动词指动作，respiratory 则描述结构或功能。

entries.definition: A mask or machine for supplying or filtering air; a countable object.
entries.definitionCN: 供气或滤气的面罩或机器，是可数物件。

entries.definition: Relating to sweating; it shares the spirare root but concerns water loss through skin.
entries.definitionCN: 与出汗有关；共享 spirare 词根，但指经皮肤失水。

entries.definition: Relating specifically to the lungs; respiratory covers nose, throat, trachea and lungs.
entries.definitionCN: 专指肺；respiratory 覆盖鼻、咽喉、气管与肺。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for the action; respiratory is the technical adjective used in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 日常词；respiratory 是医学中使用的专业形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to the mechanical movement of air; it stresses flow rather than gas exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 与空气的机械流动有关，强调流量而非气体交换。

entries.definition: Relating to the bronchi; it is narrower than respiratory.
entries.definitionCN: 与支气管有关，比 respiratory 范围窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: respire + -atory 'relating to': the adjective of breathing.
normal.cn: respire + -atory「与……有关」：呼吸的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs respire, respiration, respirator, respirometer and cardiorespiratory.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 respire、respiration、respirator、respirometer、cardiorespiratory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: respiratory system, respiratory tract, respiratory failure, respiratory rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：呼吸系统、呼吸道、呼吸衰竭、呼吸频率。

normal.en: pulmonary is only the lungs; respiratory covers the whole route.
normal.cn: pulmonary 只指肺，respiratory 覆盖整条通路。

normal.en: spirare also gives spirit, inspire and expire.
normal.cn: spirare 还衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire。

abstract.en: Picture a tree inside the chest, trunk splitting into branches and ending in tiny buds.
abstract.cn: 想象胸腔里长着一棵树，树干分叉成枝条，末端是细小的芽。

abstract.en: Picture air flowing down a corridor lined with moist pink walls.
abstract.cn: 想象空气沿着一条湿润的粉红色走廊向下流。

abstract.en: Picture a mask over a face, with a tube supplying clean air.
abstract.cn: 想象一张面罩罩住脸，管子送来洁净空气。

examples.en: Respiratory infections spread easily in crowded rooms.
examples.cn: 呼吸道感染在拥挤的房间里容易传播。

examples.en: The respiratory tract warms and moistens the air it carries.
examples.cn: 呼吸道会温暖并湿润它所输送的空气。

examples.en: Doctors watch the respiratory rate for early signs of trouble.
examples.cn: 医生监测呼吸频率以发现早期问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「respire 呼吸 + atory 的」——与呼吸有关的 → respiratory 呼吸的

root: 拉丁 spirare「呼吸」→ respirare「再次呼吸」→ respiratio「呼吸」→ 拉丁形容词 respiratorius → 英语 respiratory。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: an adjective of breathing attaches to the act, to the whole system, to the organs, to the tube, and to the diseases and measurements of that tube.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：表示呼吸的形容词依次附着于动作、整套系统、器官、管道，以及这条管道上的疾病与测量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branching passage from nose to alveoli, carrying air in and out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从鼻到肺泡的分叉通道，把空气送进送出。

branches.en: ACT AND ORGAN: the adjective can describe breathing itself or the lungs and gills that perform it.
branches.cn: 动作与器官：这个形容词既可描述呼吸本身，也可描述执行呼吸的肺与鳃。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND ROUTE: the whole set of organs and the tube through which air travels.
branches.cn: 系统与路径：整套器官以及空气经过的管道。

branches.en: WHEN IT GOES WRONG: disease and failure are the clinical face of the same adjective.
branches.cn: 出问题时：疾病与衰竭是同一形容词的临床面孔。

branches.en: THE MEASURED BREATH: respiratory rate turns breathing into a number on a chart.
branches.cn: 可测量的呼吸：呼吸频率把呼吸变成图表上的数字。

branches.en: THE BLOOD SIDE: respiratory acidosis names the chemical consequence of poor ventilation.
branches.cn: 血液一端：呼吸性酸中毒命名通气不良的化学后果。

intro.en: Respiratory is a Latin noun of breathing plus the functional adjective suffix -ory: respirat- + -ory.
intro.cn: respiratory 是拉丁「呼吸」名词加功能形容词后缀 -ory：respirat- + -ory。

latinIntro.en: Latin respirare and respiratio give English respire, respiration, respirator and respiratory; spirare also underlies spirit, inspire and expire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 respirare 与 respiratio 给出英语 respire、respiration、respirator、respiratory；spirare 还支撑 spirit、inspire、expire。

definition_en: a feeling of overwhelming joy that carries a person beyond ordinary self-control; a trance in which the mind seems to stand outside the body

intro.en: Ecstasy is Greek ekstasis, from ek- meaning out and histanai meaning to make stand, so literally a standing outside oneself; it first named a trance in which the soul leaves the body, then softened into overwhelming joy.
intro.cn: ecstasy 来自希腊语 ekstasis，由 ek-（出）与 histanai（使站立）组成，字面就是「站到自身之外」；它最初指灵魂离开身体的出神状态，后来才软化为压倒性的喜悦。

items.en: Greek histanai means to make something stand.
items.cn: 希腊语 histanai 意为使站立。

items.en: Greek ekstasis joins ek- meaning out to stasis, a standing outside oneself.
items.cn: 希腊语 ekstasis 把 ek-（出）与 stasis 结合，意为「站到自身之外」。

items.en: Latin extasis kept the sense of a trance or a seizure.
items.cn: 拉丁语 extasis 保留了出神与发作的含义。

items.en: English first used it for the soul leaving the body in prayer.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指祈祷中灵魂离开身体的状态。

items.en: The word softened into overwhelming delight.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐软化为压倒性的喜悦。

items.en: The word became a street name for a party drug.
items.cn: 这个词成为某种聚会毒品的街头名称。

note.en: Ecstasy, stasis and static all carry sta-, the Greek root for standing; ecstasy is standing outside yourself, stasis is standing still.
note.cn: ecstasy、stasis 与 static 都带 sta-，那是希腊语的「站立」；ecstasy 是站到自身之外，stasis 是站着不动。

dict_mnemonic.text: ecstasy ＝ ec-（＝ ex-，出）＋ stas（站立，希腊语 histanai）＋ -y ＝「站到自身之外」。古希腊人认为极度喜悦或宗教出神时，灵魂会离开身体站在外面，所以 ekstasis 先是「出神、灵魂离体」，后来才专指「狂喜」。同根 stasis 是「停滞、站着不动」，static 是「静止的」，ecstatic 是「狂喜的」，副词 ecstatically。搭配 in ecstasy（狂喜地／出神地）、pure ecstasy、a state of ecstasy、religious ecstasy；复数 ecstasies 指一阵阵狂喜。近义 rapture 强调「被带走」，bliss 强调圆满的幸福，trance 强调恍惚半睡。注意二十世纪起这个词成为某种聚会毒品的街头名，阅读时按上下文区分「狂喜」与「摇头丸」。

definition_zh: 内在本质的；本身价值的；内在动机的；内禀的；内部的（肌肉）；内蕴的（曲率）；本征的（半导体）；内生的（增长）
definition_en: belonging to the inner nature of a thing and measured without reference to anything outside it
core_image: 拍卖台上摆着一幅无人出价的旧素描，鉴定师却只说它的价值不在标签上
scene: 拍卖行把一幅无人问津的旧素描摆上台面，鉴定师却说它的分量不在价签上。 The old sketch has an intrinsic worth that no auction price can measure.
sceneCN: 这里指事物自身所具有、不由外界定价的价值（第 2 个义项：不依赖外部评价的内在价值）；句意为这幅旧素描有一种拍卖价量不出的内在价值。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「本质上；就其自身而言」
由该形容词的词干加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「内在性；固有性」，多用于哲学
由对应的拉丁「在外」形式进入英语，义为「外在的；外来的」，是与目标词成对的反义对照词

senses.title: Belonging to a thing's own nature
senses.definition: forming part of what something is in itself, independent of how others regard it
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物自身之所是，与别人如何看待它无关
senses.example: Curiosity seems intrinsic to the human mind.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心似乎是人心本身固有的。
senses.why: The Latin word meant 'on the inside', so a quality located within a thing's own nature is intrinsic.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词意为「在内侧」，因此位于事物自身本性之中的性质就是内在的。

senses.title: Worth that is not set by a market
senses.definition: value that a thing has in itself, apart from price, usefulness or what buyers will pay
senses.definitionCN: 事物自身即有的价值，与价格、用途或买家的出价无关
senses.example: Philosophers debate whether art has intrinsic value.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家争论艺术是否具有内在价值。
senses.why: If worth is inside the thing, then an outside price can measure it only indirectly, if at all.
senses.whyCN: 如果价值在事物内部，那么外部价格至多只能间接地量到它。

senses.title: Drive that comes from within
senses.definition: motivation arising from interest or enjoyment rather than from external reward or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 由兴趣或乐趣产生的动机，而非来自外部奖励或压力
senses.example: Intrinsic motivation keeps volunteers coming back.
senses.exampleCN: 内在动机让志愿者一再回来。
senses.why: The source of the drive sits inside the person, which is exactly what the word locates inside.
senses.whyCN: 动力的源头在人的内部，而这正是这个词所定位的「内侧」。

senses.title: A property independent of amount
senses.titleCN: 与数量多少无关的性质
senses.definition: in physics, a property of a material that does not change when the sample size changes
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中不随样品大小改变的材料性质
senses.example: Density is intrinsic; mass is not.
senses.exampleCN: 密度是内禀性质，质量不是。
senses.why: A property that stays the same whether you take a gram or a tonne belongs to the substance itself.
senses.whyCN: 无论取一克还是一吨都不变的性质，属于物质自身。

senses.title: Muscles lying inside an organ
senses.definition: in anatomy, said of muscles whose origin and insertion lie within the structure they move
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学中起止点都位于其所运动结构内部的肌肉
senses.example: The intrinsic muscles of the hand control the fingers finely.
senses.exampleCN: 手部内在肌精细地控制手指。
senses.why: Anatomy contrasts muscles inside an organ with ones that enter it from outside.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把器官内部的肌肉与从外部伸入的肌肉相对照。

senses.title: Curvature measurable from inside
senses.definition: in geometry, a curvature determined by measurements within the surface itself, without embedding it in a larger space
senses.definitionCN: 几何中只靠曲面内部的测量即可确定的曲率，无需把曲面嵌入更大空间
senses.example: Intrinsic curvature can be detected by triangles on the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 内蕴曲率可以通过曲面上的三角形测出。
senses.why: If the measurement needs nothing outside, the property is literally intrinsic to the surface.
senses.whyCN: 若测量不需要任何外部条件，该性质就字面地内在于曲面之中。

senses.title: Pure, undoped material
senses.definition: in electronics, said of a semiconductor whose behaviour comes from its own pure crystal, with no added impurities
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中行为来自纯净晶体本身、未添加杂质的半导体
senses.example: Intrinsic silicon conducts far less than doped silicon.
senses.exampleCN: 本征硅的导电性远低于掺杂硅。
senses.why: Its electrical behaviour is a property of the pure material, not of anything added from outside.
senses.whyCN: 它的电学行为来自纯净材料本身，而不是外部添加物。

senses.title: Growth generated from inside
senses.definition: in economics, growth produced by internal factors such as knowledge and investment in people, not by outside shocks
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中由知识、对人的投资等内部因素产生的增长，而非外部冲击带来
senses.example: Intrinsic growth models stress education over foreign aid.
senses.exampleCN: 内生增长模型强调教育胜过外国援助。
senses.why: The model looks for the causes of growth inside the economy rather than outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这类模型在经济体内部寻找增长原因，而不是在外部寻找。

intro.en: Intrinsic comes from Late Latin intrinsecus 'inwardly, on the inside', built on intra 'within' and secus 'alongside'. French intrinsèque carried it into English in the seventeenth century, paired with extrinsic. The direct source is clear; the earlier makeup of secus is still debated.
intro.cn: intrinsic 来自晚期拉丁 intrinsecus「向内的、在内侧的」，由 intra「在内」与 secus「沿着、旁边」构成。法语 intrinsèque 在十七世纪把它带进英语，并与 extrinsic 成对。直接来源清楚；更早的 secus 构成仍有争议。

items.en: Intra meant within or inside, and it still appears in English words such as intravenous.
items.cn: intra 意为在……之内，至今出现在 intravenous 等英语词中。

items.en: Secus meant alongside or beside; its further origin is disputed, so the internal makeup of the compound is not certain.
items.cn: secus 意为沿着、在旁边；它更早的来源有争议，因此这个复合词的内部构成并非确证。

items.en: The adverb meant inward or on the inside, and it described what belongs to a thing from within.
items.cn: 这个副词意为向内、在内侧，描述从内部属于某物的东西。

items.en: Its partner meant from outside, and the pair intrinsic and extrinsic still divide inner nature from external circumstance.
items.cn: 与之配对的形式意为「从外部」，如今「内在」与「外在」这一对仍用于区分本性与外部环境。

items.en: English took intrinsic through French for qualities belonging to a thing itself, especially in philosophy and theology.
items.cn: 英语经法语引入这个词，用于属于事物自身的性质，尤其在哲学与神学中。

items.en: Physics, anatomy, geometry and economics each gave the word a measured meaning where 'inside' can be tested.
items.cn: 物理学、解剖学、几何学与经济学各自给这个词一个可检验的「内部」含义。

note.en: The first group is the same word family with its opposite; the second group holds near synonyms that locate qualities differently.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族及其对立词；第二组是同样描述性质归属、但定位方式不同的近义词。

entries.definition: By its own nature, without reference to outside standards; it marks the source of value.
entries.definitionCN: 就其自身本性而言，不参照外部标准；标出价值的来源。

entries.definition: The quality of belonging to a thing's inner nature; a rare philosophical noun.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物内在本性的性质；少见的哲学名词。

entries.definition: Coming from outside, such as reward, price or circumstance; the exact opposite partner.
entries.definitionCN: 来自外部的东西，如奖励、价格或环境；正是与之相对的另一半。

entries.definition: An older variant spelling of the same adjective, now mostly replaced by the shorter form.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较早异体拼法，如今多被较短的形取代。

entries.definition: Stuck to a subject so that it cannot be removed; it stresses attachment, while the target word stresses inner nature.
entries.definitionCN: 附着于主体而无法去除；强调「附着」，而目标词强调「内在本质」。

entries.definition: Present from birth; it marks a starting point in time rather than a location inside a nature.
entries.definitionCN: 出生时即有；标出时间上的起点，而非本性内部的位置。

entries.definition: Belonging to the essence, so that without it the thing would not be itself; stronger than a mere inner quality.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本质，缺了它事物就不成其为自身；比单纯「内在性质」更强。

entries.definition: Designed into a product; the everyday word for what is installed rather than grown from within.
entries.definitionCN: 设计进产品里的；是日常说法，指装进去而非从内部长出来的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'within': intrinsic value is the value inside the thing, not on the price tag.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在内」：内在价值是事物里面的价值，不在价签上。

normal.en: The family runs intrinsically, intrinsicality and the paired opposite extrinsic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本质上、内在性，以及与它成对的外在的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark value and drive: intrinsic value, intrinsic motivation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出价值与动力：内在价值、内在动机。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark science: intrinsic property, intrinsic semiconductor.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：内禀性质、本征半导体。

normal.en: Its opposite is extrinsic, which puts the source outside the thing.
normal.cn: 它的对立词是 extrinsic，把来源放在事物外部。

abstract.en: Picture a coin whose shine comes from its own metal, not the light in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币的光泽来自它自己的金属，而不是房间里的灯。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who trains because the running itself feels good.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者训练，因为跑这件事本身让他舒服。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose warmth comes from its stones, not from a heater.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子的暖意来自石头本身，而不是暖气。

examples.en: The painting's intrinsic value lies in its brushwork, not its price.
examples.cn: 这幅画的内在价值在笔法，而不在价格。

examples.en: Children learn faster when motivation is intrinsic.
examples.cn: 当动机来自内心时，孩子学得更快。

examples.en: Conductivity is an intrinsic property of the pure crystal.
examples.cn: 导电性是纯晶体的内禀性质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印吹壳」——印在壳子最里面那一层，从外看不见，就是内在的

root: 拉丁 intra「在内」+ secus「沿着、旁边」→ 晚期拉丁 intrinsecus「内侧的」→ 法语 intrinsèque → 英语 intrinsic；与 extrinsecus「外在的」成对。secus 的更早来源尚有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place a quality inside its owner: in a nature, a value, a motive, a material property, an organ, a surface, a crystal or an economy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某种性质放在所有者内部：放在本性里、价值里、动机里、材料性质里、器官里、曲面里、晶体里，或经济体里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quality that lives inside a thing, so outside measures can only approach it.
core.cn: 核心意象：住在事物内部的一种性质，外部量度只能靠近它。

branches.en: THE NATURE SENSE: what a thing is in itself, apart from outside opinion.
branches.cn: 本性义：某物自身之所是，与外部看法无关。

branches.en: THE VALUED AND MOTIVATED SIDE: worth not set by a market, and interest that needs no reward.
branches.cn: 价值与动力一面：不由市场定价的价值，以及无需奖励的兴趣。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL SIDE: properties unchanged by sample size, and the behaviour of a pure crystal.
branches.cn: 材料一面：不随样品大小改变的性质，以及纯晶体自身的行为。

branches.en: THE ANATOMICAL SIDE: muscles whose ends both lie inside the organ they move.
branches.cn: 解剖一面：两端都在所运动器官内部的肌肉。

branches.en: THE SELF-CONTAINED SIDE: curvature measured within a surface, and growth generated inside an economy.
branches.cn: 自足一面：在曲面内部测得的曲率，以及经济体内部产生的增长。

intro.en: Intrinsic is a Latin adverb turned adjective: intra 'within' plus secus 'alongside', with the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: intrinsic 是由拉丁副词转成的形容词：intra「在内」加 secus「沿着」，再加形容词词尾 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Intra plus secus gives the adverb intrinsecus 'inwardly'; the adjective form, through French, is intrinsèque, taken into English as intrinsic.
latinIntro.cn: intra 加 secus 得出副词 intrinsecus「向内」；其形容词形式经法语作 intrinsèque，进入英语成为 intrinsic。

items.example: The prefix locates the quality inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把性质定位在内部。

items.example: Its earlier origin is disputed, so the compound is not fully certain.
items.exampleCN: 它更早的来源有争议，因此该复合词并非完全确证。

items.example: The adverb is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词是形容词的直接来源。

items.example: The counterpart gives the paired opposite in English.
items.exampleCN: 配对形式给出英语中的反义对照词。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把副词变成形容词。

items.example: English added measurable technical senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语加上了可量度的技术义。

items.example: The ending gives the manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾给出方式副词。

items.example: The suffix names the inner quality in philosophy.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀在哲学中命名「内在性」。

items.example: The longer form is now archaic.
items.exampleCN: 较长的形式如今已属古旧。

items.example: The opposite partner appears in the same technical fields.
items.exampleCN: 这个对立词出现在同一批技术领域。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「本质上」
由该形容词词干加性质名词后缀构成，义为「内在性」
由对应的「在外」形式进入英语，义为「外在的」

definition_zh: 债权人；放贷方；账面上的应付对象；债权国
definition_en: a person, firm or country to whom money is owed and who has a claim on the debtor
core_image: 清算桌上，一叠文件依次被盖章，每个印章下面写着一个可以收回的数目
scene: 清算会议上，各方依次在文件上盖章，确认各自可以收回的金额。 The creditor refused the offer and demanded full payment.
sceneCN: 这里 creditor 指「债权人」（第 1 个义项：被欠款、对债务人享有请求权的一方）；句意为这名债权人拒绝了方案，要求全额偿付。图中可辨识物件：清算文件、印章、金额栏、编号标签。

pos.zh: 债权人；放贷方；债权国（可数）

senses.title: A person to whom money is owed
senses.definition: a person or firm that has a right to receive payment from a debtor
senses.definitionCN: 有权向债务人收取款项的个人或公司
senses.example: The creditor refused the offer and demanded full payment.
senses.exampleCN: 这名债权人拒绝了方案，要求全额偿付。
senses.why: creditor is the Latin agent noun of credere 'to trust': the one who trusted another with money and now holds a claim.
senses.whyCN: creditor 是拉丁 credere「信任」的施事名词：把钱托付给他人信任、如今握有请求权的那一方。

senses.title: A lending institution
senses.definition: a bank or finance house that holds loans and is owed repayment
senses.definitionCN: 持有贷款、有权要求偿还的银行或金融公司
senses.example: The bank became the largest creditor in the restructuring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行成为重组中最大的债权人。
senses.why: an institution that lends stands in the same legal position as a private lender, so the same noun applies.
senses.whyCN: 放贷机构与私人出借人处于同一法律地位，因此适用同一个名词。

senses.title: A supplier shown in accounts
senses.definition: in bookkeeping, a person or firm to whom the business owes money for goods or services, listed among creditors
senses.definitionCN: 记账上企业因货物或服务而欠款、被列入债权人项下的个人或公司
senses.example: Trade creditors were paid within thirty days.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易债权人于三十天内获得付款。
senses.why: British accounts call the whole payables side creditors, because every unpaid supplier holds a claim.
senses.whyCN: 英国账务把整个应付一侧称为债权人，因为每个未获付款的供货方都握有请求权。

senses.title: A sovereign creditor
senses.definition: a state or international institution that has lent to another government
senses.definitionCN: 向另一国政府放贷的国家或国际机构
senses.example: Foreign creditors agreed to a longer repayment period.
senses.exampleCN: 外国债权国同意延长偿还期限。
senses.why: states lend and are owed like banks, so the word scales to the level of a treasury.
senses.whyCN: 国家像银行一样放贷并被欠款，因此这个词可放大到国库层面。

senses.title: A claimant in law
senses.definition: in insolvency or civil law, a party with a provable claim against another's assets
senses.definitionCN: 在破产或民事法律中，对他方财产享有可证明请求权的一方
senses.example: The creditor filed a claim before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 债权人在截止日前申报了债权。
senses.why: law needs a neutral name for anyone with a money claim, whether or not a loan created it.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个中性名称来指任何拥有金钱请求权的人，无论该请求权是否由借贷产生。

senses.title: One owed gratitude, figuratively
senses.definition: figuratively, a person to whom one owes thanks or recognition
senses.definitionCN: 比喻上指某人欠其感谢或承认的人
senses.example: The whole school is a creditor of the old gardener's care.
senses.exampleCN: 整个学校都欠这位老园丁一份照料之情。
senses.why: if a favour is a loan, the one who gave it holds the claim, so a benefactor becomes a creditor.
senses.whyCN: 若恩惠是贷款，给出恩惠者就握有请求权，因此恩人成了债权人。

senses.title: A supplier who grants credit
senses.definition: a seller who delivers goods before payment and so holds a claim for the price
senses.definitionCN: 先交货后收款、因而对价款享有请求权的一方
senses.example: The paper merchant acted as creditor for the whole term.
senses.exampleCN: 这家纸张商在整个学期里充当赊账债权人。
senses.why: credit sales are loans in kind, and the unpaid seller occupies the creditor's position.
senses.whyCN: 赊销是实物形式的贷款，未获付款的卖方占据债权人的位置。

senses.title: One who trusted money to another, historically
senses.titleCN: 旧时因信任而放贷的人
senses.definition: historically, a person who entrusted money or goods to another on the strength of trust in repayment
senses.definitionCN: 历史上凭对偿还的信任把钱或货物交给他人的人
senses.example: The old creditor kept a private book of every promise.
senses.exampleCN: 这位旧时债权人把每一个承诺都记在私人册子上。
senses.why: the Latin verb behind the word means to trust, so the earliest creditor was simply someone who trusted a borrower.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁动词意为信任，因此最早的债权人就是信任借款人的那个人。

intro.en: Creditor comes straight from Latin creditor, the agent noun of credere 'to trust, entrust'. The word has always carried both trust and money. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: creditor 直接来自拉丁 creditor，即 credere「信任、托付」的施事名词。这个词一直同时带着信任与金钱两层意思。年代均为约数。

items.en: Credere meant 'to trust, believe, entrust'. It is the source of creed, credit, credible and credential as well as creditor.
items.cn: credere 意为「信任、相信、托付」，是 creed、credit、credible、credential 以及 creditor 的来源。

items.en: The common account of credere as a compound of a word for 'heart' plus dare 'to give', literally 'to give one's heart', is a hypothesis and not an established derivation.
items.cn: 把 credere 解释为「心」加 dare「给」、字面为「把心交出」的说法只是假说，并非已确立的派生。

items.en: Creditor was the agent noun for the one who trusted another with money, and it was used in Roman accounts and law.
items.cn: creditor 是施事名词，指把钱托付给他人信任的人，用于罗马的账务与法律。

items.en: Old French crediteur carried the word into English in the Middle Ages, first in legal and commercial writing.
items.cn: 古法语 crediteur 在中世纪把这个词带入英语，最先用于法律与商业文书。

items.en: From the nineteenth century British bookkeeping used creditors for the payables side, giving the word a collective sense.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，英国记账用 creditors 指应付一侧，使这个词有了集合义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the exact first English use is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of credere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语中最早用例没有定论，credere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the trust-and-credit stem; group two holds the parties and instruments that surround a claim.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「信任与信用」词干的形式；第二组是围绕债权存在的各方与工具。

entries.definition: The trust that allows deferred payment, or an entry on the right side of a ledger; not the party.
entries.definitionCN: 允许延期付款的信任，或账簿右侧的分录；不是当事人。

entries.definition: Believable or convincing; it shares the trust root but says nothing about money.
entries.definitionCN: 可信的、有说服力的；共用信任词根，但与金钱无关。

entries.definition: A document or qualification that shows one may be trusted in a role.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某人可被信任担任某角色的文件或资历。

entries.definition: A statement of belief, from the same verb but with no financial sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 信仰声明，同出这一动词，但完全没有金融义。

entries.definition: The one who owes; creditor and debtor are the two ends of one obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 欠债的一方；债权人与债务人是同一义务的两端。

entries.definition: The party who gave the money; every lender becomes a creditor while the loan is unpaid.
entries.definitionCN: 交付款项的一方；贷款未清时每个出借人都是债权人。

entries.definition: The owner of a bond, which is a tradable claim on the issuer; a creditor by another route.
entries.definitionCN: 债券持有人，债券是对发行人的可转让请求权；以另一条路径成为债权人。

entries.definition: A person who asserts a right, often in court; not all claimants are creditors.
entries.definitionCN: 主张某项权利的人，常在法庭上；并非所有主张者都是债权人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cred- is 'trust': a creditor is the one who trusted another with money.
normal.cn: cred- 意为「信任」：债权人就是把钱托付给他人信任的人。

normal.en: The family runs credit, creditor, credible, credibility, credential and creditworthy.
normal.cn: 同族包括 credit、creditor、credible、credibility、credential 与 creditworthy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a secured creditor, an unsecured creditor, a creditors' meeting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：有担保债权人、无担保债权人、债权人会议。

normal.en: Creditor and debtor are mirror terms: one is owed, one owes.
normal.cn: creditor 与 debtor 是一对镜像词：一个被欠，一个欠。

normal.en: In British accounts the payables side is simply called creditors.
normal.cn: 在英国账务中，应付一侧就径直称为债权人。

abstract.en: Picture a row of stamps coming down on a page, each marking a claim.
abstract.cn: 想象一排印章落在同一页上，每个都标记一项请求权。

abstract.en: Picture a benefactor holding a receipt for a kindness.
abstract.cn: 想象一位恩人手里握着一张善意的收据。

abstract.en: Picture trust as the string that turns a giver into a claimant.
abstract.cn: 想象信任是那根绳子，把给出者变成请求权人。

examples.en: Secured creditors are paid before shareholders.
examples.cn: 有担保债权人先于股东获得偿付。

examples.en: The country's foreign creditors accepted a write-off.
examples.cn: 该国的外国债权人接受了债务减记。

examples.en: Every unpaid supplier is a creditor of the firm.
examples.cn: 每个未获付款的供货方都是这家公司的债权人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「credit（信用）+ or（人）」——凭信用把钱借出、等着收回的人 → 债权人

root: 拉丁 creditor「信任而放贷者」，来自 credere「信任、托付」；credere 更深来源不确定，将其解为「心 + 给」仅为假说。英语经古法语 crediteur 借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one position: the party who trusted another with value and now holds a claim, whether a private lender, a bank, a supplier, a state, a litigant, a benefactor or an old moneylender.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个位置展开：把价值托付他人信任、如今握有请求权的一方，可以是私人出借人、银行、供货方、国家、诉讼当事人、恩人，或旧时放债者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of seals on a claims page, each beside a sum to be recovered.
core.cn: 核心意象：请求权页面上的一排印章，每个印章旁写着一笔待收回的金额。

branches.en: THE PERSON WHO TRUSTED: the modern claimant and the old trusting lender are the same figure.
branches.cn: 托付信任的人：现代请求权人与旧时凭信任放贷者是同一个人物。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: a bank stands in the same legal position as a private lender.
branches.cn: 机构：银行与私人出借人处于同一法律地位。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNTS: unpaid suppliers are creditors whether or not cash was lent.
branches.cn: 账目：未获付款的供货方无论是否借出过现金，都是债权人。

branches.en: STATES AND COURTS: a treasury and a litigant both assert a money claim.
branches.cn: 国家与法庭：国库与诉讼当事人都主张一项金钱请求权。

branches.en: FAVOURS: if kindness is a loan, the benefactor holds the claim.
branches.cn: 恩惠：若善意是贷款，恩人就握有请求权。

intro.en: Creditor is a Latin agent noun: a verb of trusting plus the ending that marks the one who acts.
intro.cn: creditor 是一个拉丁施事名词：一个表示信任的动词加上标记行动者的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin credere and creditum give credit, creditor, credible and credential, so one trust-root runs through the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 credere 与 creditum 衍生 credit、creditor、credible 与 credential，一个「信任」词根贯穿整个词族。

items.example: The root runs through credit and creed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根贯穿 credit 与 creed。

items.structure: credere, credidi, creditum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: To lend is to trust with value.
items.exampleCN: 放贷就是把价值托付他人信任。

items.example: The ending marks the party who holds the claim.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记握有请求权的一方。

items.meaning: one who trusts another with money
items.meaningCN: 把钱托付他人信任的人
items.example: The creditor demanded payment.
items.exampleCN: 债权人要求付款。

items.example: The supplier offered thirty days of credit.
items.exampleCN: 供货方给予三十天赊账期。

items.example: The witness gave a credible account.
items.exampleCN: 证人提供了可信的叙述。

items.example: The report damaged the agency's credibility.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告损害了该机构的可信度。

items.meaning: evidence that one may be trusted
items.example: The board checked her credentials.
items.exampleCN: 董事会核验了她的资历。

items.meaning: fit to be trusted with credit

definition_zh: 大批毁灭；严重削弱；杀死十分之一（古义）
definition_en: to destroy a large proportion of something, or in the old Roman sense to kill one in every ten
core_image: 一排士兵抽签，每十个人里有一人向前一步，走向另一侧
scene: 一场疫病过后，村里的羊只剩不到三成。 The epidemic decimated the herd within a single season.
sceneCN: 这里 decimate 指疫病大批杀死牲畜、使群体所剩无几（第 1 个义项：大批毁灭）；句意为这场疫病在一个季节内就让羊群大批死亡。

senses.title: Destroy a large proportion
senses.definition: to kill or destroy a large part of a group or population
senses.definitionCN: 杀死或毁掉一个群体或人口中的大部分
senses.example: The epidemic decimated the herd within a single season.
senses.exampleCN: 这场疫病在一个季节内就让羊群大批死亡。
senses.why: The Roman punishment took one in ten; over time the word's force grew until it meant a heavy loss rather than an exact tenth.
senses.whyCN: 罗马的惩罚是十人杀一；随着时间推移，这个词的力度增大，指惨重损失，而不再指精确的十分之一。

senses.title: Severely weaken
senses.definition: to reduce the strength or effectiveness of something drastically
senses.definitionCN: 大幅降低某物的力量或效力
senses.example: The scandal decimated the party's credibility.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻严重削弱了该党的公信力。
senses.why: A group can be hit without being killed: when every tenth member is removed, the remaining body cannot work as before.
senses.whyCN: 群体可以被打击而不被杀死：每十人中失去一人，剩下的身体也无法像从前那样运作。

senses.title: The Roman punishment
senses.definition: in Roman history, to kill one soldier in every ten as a unit punishment
senses.definitionCN: 在罗马史中，作为部队惩罚，每十名士兵处死一名
senses.example: The legion was decimated after the mutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 哗变之后，这个军团被施以十一抽杀。
senses.why: The original sense is exact: decem is ten, and the punishment was counted out one by one.
senses.whyCN: 原义是精确的：decem 就是十，惩罚是一个一个数出来的。

senses.title: Devastate by disease or war
senses.titleCN: 疫病或战争造成大量死亡
senses.definition: of disease, war or disaster, to kill many members of a population
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病、战争或灾难使人口大量死亡
senses.example: Smallpox decimated the villages along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 天花使沿河的村庄人口大减。
senses.why: When the cause is invisible, the arithmetic is still visible in the empty houses left behind.
senses.whyCN: 当原因看不见时，算术仍留在空置的房屋里。

senses.title: Take a tenth, in old use
senses.definition: in older use, to take a tenth of something, especially as a tax
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，取走某物的十分之一，尤指作为税
senses.example: The old chronicle says the ruler decimated the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 旧编年史说统治者抽取了收成的十分之一。
senses.why: The word carries both a fraction and a blow: a tenth can be a lawful share or a lethal cut, depending on who counts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词同时带着分数与打击：十分之一可以是合法份额，也可以是致命削减，取决于谁来数。

senses.title: Thin out a group
senses.definition: to remove a large number of members from a group, often at random
senses.definitionCN: 从群体中大量移除成员，常带有随机性
senses.example: The layoffs decimated the research division.
senses.exampleCN: 裁员让研究部门的人数锐减。
senses.why: Removal at random feels like a lottery, which is close to the original punishment's method of choosing.
senses.whyCN: 随机移除感觉像抽签，这与原初惩罚的挑选方式相近。

senses.title: Ruin a place
senses.definition: of a place, to damage it so severely that little remains intact
senses.definitionCN: 指把某地破坏到几乎不剩完整之物
senses.example: Repeated fires decimated the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 反复的火灾毁掉了这座老城。
senses.why: A place is a collection of structures and people; remove enough of either and the whole stops functioning as a town.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方是建筑与人的集合；移除其中任何一方足够多，整体就不再作为城镇运作。

senses.title: Shrink a population in ecology
senses.definition: in ecology, to reduce a population sharply, often below a viable level
senses.definitionCN: 在生态学中，使种群骤减，常低于可维持水平
senses.example: Invasive species decimated the native frogs.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵物种使本地蛙类数量骤减。
senses.why: A population needs a minimum number to breed and recover; below that line, a heavy loss becomes a permanent one.
senses.whyCN: 种群需要最低数量才能繁殖与恢复；低于这条线，惨重损失就变成永久损失。

intro.en: Decimate comes from the Latin word for ten and originally named a Roman punishment of one in ten.
intro.cn: decimate 来自拉丁语中表示「十」的词，最初命名罗马「十人杀一」的惩罚。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 17c. for the Roman punishment, and by the 19c. it was used for any heavy loss.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个动词，指罗马的惩罚；到十九世纪，它已用于任何惨重损失。

items.en: Decimare meant 'to take a tenth' and, in the army, 'to punish by killing one in ten'.
items.cn: decimare 意为「取十分之一」，在军队中意为「以十人杀一的方式惩罚」。

items.en: Decem is the Latin word for ten, the source of decimal and December, the tenth month of the old calendar.
items.cn: decem 是拉丁语「十」，是 decimal 与 December（旧历的第十个月）的来源。

items.en: A unit that had disgraced itself was divided into groups of ten and each group drew lots for one to be beaten or killed.
items.cn: 蒙羞的部队被分成十人一组，每组抽签选出一人受鞭打或处死。

items.en: Usage guides long argued that the word should mean exactly one in ten, but the wider sense of heavy loss now dominates.
items.cn: 用法指南长期主张这个词应精确表示「十分之一」，但如今「惨重损失」的宽泛义已占主导。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ten root; the near-meaning group names kinds of large destruction.
note.cn: 形近组共享「十」词根；近义组列出大规模毁灭的各种方式。

definition_zh: 熟练的；精通的；（语言）达到工作水平的
definition_en: able to do something well and effectively, at a level good enough for real work
core_image: 一位乐手不看谱也能把整段协奏曲拉完，手指在弦上几乎没有停顿
scene: 排练时乐手不看谱便把整段协奏曲拉完，指挥只偶尔点头。 By her third year she was proficient on the cello.
sceneCN: 乐手三年后不看谱也能完整拉完协奏曲；句中的 proficient 指「熟练到足以实际运用」（第 1 个义项：在真实任务中能独立做好）。图中可辨识物件：大提琴、弓、谱架、节拍器。

senses.title: Skilled enough for real work
senses.definition: able to carry out a task well without close supervision
senses.definitionCN: 能在没有密切监督的情况下把任务做好
senses.example: By her third year she was proficient on the cello.
senses.exampleCN: 到第三年，她已经能熟练地演奏大提琴。
senses.why: proficere means 'to make progress', so the adjective marks someone who has got far enough to work, not someone who has merely begun.
senses.whyCN: proficere 意为「取得进展」，因此这个形容词标记的是已经走到能做事的人，而不是刚刚起步的人。

senses.title: A working level in a language
senses.definition: able to use a language for ordinary professional or academic purposes
senses.definitionCN: 能把一种语言用于日常的职业或学术目的
senses.example: He is proficient in English and can chair a meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他英语熟练，能够主持会议。
senses.why: language testing fixed the adjective at a working band: enough to function, not necessarily native-like.
senses.whyCN: 语言测试把这个形容词固定在「工作水平」这一档：足以运转，不必像母语者。

senses.title: Technically skilled
senses.definition: practised in the use of a tool, instrument or technique
senses.definitionCN: 在使用工具、仪器或技法方面经过练习
senses.example: The lab hires only proficient technicians.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室只聘用熟练的技术员。
senses.why: the adjective attaches easily to tools because skill with a tool can be seen at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词很容易与工具连用，因为用工具的技艺一看便知。

senses.title: An advanced learner, as a noun
senses.titleCN: 名词用法：学有所成者（罕用）
senses.definition: a person who has reached an advanced level, especially in a language
senses.definitionCN: 达到较高水平的人，尤指在语言方面
senses.example: The class moved the proficients into a separate reading group.
senses.exampleCN: 班上把学有所成者分进另一个阅读组。
senses.why: the rare noun turns the adjective into a person, a usage kept alive mainly in language teaching.
senses.whyCN: 罕用的名词用法把形容词变成人，这种用法主要活在语言教学里。

senses.title: Effective in practice
senses.definition: doing what is needed competently rather than merely knowing about it
senses.definitionCN: 把需要的事做得像样，而不只是知道怎么做
senses.example: A proficient manager settles the dispute before it spreads.
senses.exampleCN: 一位称职的管理者会在争执扩散前把它解决。
senses.why: the word always points at performance: proficiency is shown in what gets done, not in what is claimed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始终指向实际表现：熟练显现在做成的事上，而非宣称上。

senses.title: Showing mastery in performance
senses.definition: performing with control and assurance that practice has produced
senses.definitionCN: 以练习带来的控制力与把握完成表演
senses.example: Her proficient handling of the difficult passage drew applause.
senses.exampleCN: 她处理那段难句时显出功力，赢得掌声。
senses.why: in the arts the adjective praises control: the notes are not merely correct but securely held.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术中，这个形容词称赞的是控制力：音符不仅正确，而且握得稳。

senses.title: Trained and qualified
senses.definition: having completed the training that a role requires
senses.definitionCN: 已完成某个岗位所要求的训练
senses.example: Only proficient operators may run the press.
senses.exampleCN: 只有熟练的操作员才能开这台压机。
senses.why: qualification adds a gate: training ends when a person is judged proficient enough to be trusted alone.
senses.whyCN: 「合格」加上一道闸门：训练在一人被判定熟练到可以独自负责时结束。

senses.title: Capable but not an expert
senses.definition: good enough for the task at hand while falling short of mastery
senses.definitionCN: 足以应付眼前任务，但尚未达到精通
senses.example: He is proficient, though not yet expert, at repairing watches.
senses.exampleCN: 他修表已算熟练，但还称不上专家。
senses.why: the comparative scale leaves room above proficient; the word marks a threshold passed, not a summit reached.
senses.whyCN: 比较级量表在 proficient 之上还留有空间；这个词标记的是已过的门槛，而非登上的顶峰。

intro.en: Proficient is the present participle of Latin proficere 'to make progress, accomplish', built on pro- 'forward' and facere 'to do, make'. It entered English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: proficient 是拉丁 proficere「取得进展、完成」的现在分词，由 pro-「向前」与 facere「做、造」构成，于十六世纪进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Facere 'to do, make' is the root behind fact, effect, defect and every English verb in -fy.
items.cn: facere「做、造」是 fact、effect、defect 以及一切由它构成的英语动词背后的词根。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus facere gave proficere 'to make progress, to accomplish, to be of use'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 facere 给出 proficere「取得进展、完成、有用」。

items.en: The present participle proficiens described someone in the middle of making progress, hence 'getting somewhere, effective'.
items.cn: 现在分词 proficiens 描述正处在进展中的人，因此意为「走得到地方的、有效的」。

items.en: English adopted proficient in the sixteenth century, at first for things that were useful, then for people well advanced in a skill.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪采用 proficient，先指事物有用，后指人在技能上进展良好。

items.en: Twentieth-century language testing gave the adjective a fixed working band, so a certificate can state that someone is proficient rather than fluent.
items.cn: 二十世纪的语言测试给这个形容词一个固定的工作档位，于是证书可以写明某人为熟练而非流利。

items.en: The pre-Latin origin of facere is generally connected to a root meaning 'to put, set', but the exact chain is a reconstruction, and the sixteenth-century sense development is only partly documented.
items.cn: facere 在拉丁语之前的来源一般被认为与表示「放置」的词根相关，但确切链条属重构，十六世纪的语义发展也只有部分记录。

note.en: Group one holds the noun and the prefix siblings that look alike; group two holds adjectives of ability that claim different degrees.
note.cn: 第一组是名词形式以及形近的前缀同族词；第二组是表示能力的形容词，各自宣称的程度不同。

entries.definition: The measured level; proficient describes the person who holds it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被测出的水平；proficient 描述拥有这个水平的人。

entries.definition: Describes how a task is done, not what a person is.
entries.definitionCN: 描述任务如何被完成，而非人怎样。

entries.definition: From ex- plus facere: getting results with little waste, which says nothing about skill level.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex- 加 facere：以很少耗费取得结果，与技能水平无关。

entries.definition: From sub- plus facere: enough in amount, a quantity word rather than a skill word.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sub- 加 facere：数量上足够，是数量词而非技能词。

entries.definition: The plain adjective for training and practice; proficient adds the sense of being good enough for real work.
entries.definitionCN: 指受过训练与练习的普通形容词；proficient 多出「足以实际工作」之意。

entries.definition: Meets the required standard, sometimes no more than that; proficient usually implies a firmer command.
entries.definitionCN: 达到要求的标准，有时仅止于此；proficient 通常意味着更稳的掌控。

entries.definition: Smooth and rapid in speech, with less attention to accuracy or range than proficient.
entries.definitionCN: 说话顺滑快速，对准确度与覆盖面不如 proficient 看重。

entries.definition: A far higher claim than proficient: recognized mastery in a narrow field.
entries.definitionCN: 比 proficient 高得多的说法：在狭窄领域被认可的精通。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real Latin participle, the real family and the real threshold the word marks.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的拉丁分词、真实词族，以及这个词所标记的真实门槛。

normal.en: proficiens is a participle: someone in the middle of getting somewhere.
normal.cn: proficiens 是分词：一个正走到某处的人。

normal.en: pro- 'forward' plus facere 'do': moving forward in what one does.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」加 facere「做」：在做的事上向前走。

normal.en: The family runs proficient, proficiency, proficiently.
normal.cn: 词族包括 proficient、proficiency、proficiently。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the test: proficient in, highly proficient, proficient user.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出测试语境：在……熟练、高度熟练、熟练使用者。

normal.en: The word marks a threshold, so it pairs with enough and not yet: proficient enough, not yet expert.
normal.cn: 这个词标记门槛，因此常与「够」和「尚未」连用：够熟练、尚未精通。

abstract.cn: 想象一位乐手已不再需要看谱，却仍把谱子摊开。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked with a line at shoulder height, already passed.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在齐肩高处画了一道线，而人已走过它。

examples.en: She became proficient in Spanish after two summers abroad.
examples.cn: 在国外度过两个夏天后，她的西班牙语变得熟练。

examples.en: A proficient reader adjusts speed to the difficulty of the text.
examples.cn: 熟练的读者会按文本难度调整速度。

examples.en: The workshop produces proficient welders in six months.
examples.cn: 这个工作坊六个月就能培养出熟练的焊工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ fic（做）」——越做越往前 → 熟练的、精通的

root: 拉丁 pro-「向前」+ facere「做」→ proficere「取得进展」→ 现在分词 proficiens → 英语 proficient；facere 的更早来源一般与「放置」词根相关，确切链条属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one threshold: a learner has moved far enough forward to do real work, and the threshold is then applied to a language, a tool, a classroom role, a dispute, a performance, a licence and a repair bench.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用一个门槛：学习者向前走到足以做真实工作的位置，这个门槛随后用于语言、工具、课堂角色、争执、表演、执照与修理台。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on a doorframe at shoulder height, already crossed, with more height still available above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：门框上齐肩高处的一道线，人已跨过，而线上方仍有余地。

branches.en: THE THRESHOLD: the same line separates training from trusted independent work.
branches.cn: 门槛：同一条线把训练与可被信任的独立工作分开。

branches.en: THE LANGUAGE BAND: testing pins the threshold to a working level of a language.
branches.cn: 语言档位：测试把门槛固定在语言的工作水平上。

branches.en: HAND AND STAGE: a tool and a performance both show the threshold in execution.
branches.cn: 手与舞台：工具与表演都把门槛显现在执行之中。

branches.en: ROLE AND PRACTICE: the rare noun names the person, and effective practice proves the claim.
branches.cn: 角色与实践：罕用名词指人，有效的实践则证明这份宣称。

branches.en: ROOM ABOVE: mastery lies beyond the line, so proficient never means finished.
branches.cn: 线上余地：精通在门槛之外，因此 proficient 从不意味「到头」。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin prefix and root plus a participle ending, and the same pieces build the whole proficiency family.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由拉丁前缀、词根加一个分词词尾构成，同一批部件造出整个 proficiency 词族。

latinIntro.en: Pro- and facere build proficere; its present participle proficiens is the direct source of the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: pro- 与 facere 构成 proficere；其现在分词 proficiens 是英语形容词的直接来源。
