definition_zh: 可变性；变异性；变动幅度；（统计）离散程度
definition_en: the quality or degree of being changeable, or the extent to which values differ from one another
core_image: 同一块地的十次收成排成一列，高低差别明显，尺子量出的正是这些差别
scene: 这里指「可变性」。 Rainfall variability makes farming risky in this region.
sceneCN: 这里 variability 指「变动幅度」（第 1 个义项：随时间或个案变化、不稳定）；句意：降水量的变动使该地区的农业风险很大。图中可辨识物件：逐年降水柱状图、干裂的田块、蓄水池。

pos.zh: 可变性；变异性；变动幅度；（统计）离散程度（多为不可数，也可用 variabilities 指多种变异）

senses.title: Changeability
senses.definition: the quality of being changeable
senses.definitionCN: 容易发生变化的性质
senses.example: Rainfall variability makes farming risky in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 降水量的变化使该地区的农业风险很大。
senses.why: Varius in Latin meant 'diverse, spotted, changeable'. The noun -ability turns that quality into a measurable thing: not 'it changes' but 'how much it changes'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 varius 意为「多样的、有斑点的、易变的」。名词后缀 -ability 把这种性质变成可度量之物：不是「它变」，而是「它变得有多少」。

senses.title: Statistical Spread
senses.titleCN: 统计离散：数值彼此差多少
senses.definition: the extent to which values in a set differ from one another
senses.definitionCN: 一组数值之间相互差异的程度
senses.example: The variability of the scores was low, so the class was evenly matched.
senses.exampleCN: 分数的离散程度很低，说明这个班水平相当。
senses.why: Statistics needs a word for difference rather than average. Variability measures how far the members scatter, which is why it pairs with standard deviation and range.
senses.whyCN: 统计学需要一个词来表示「差异」而不是「平均」；variability 量的是成员分散得多远，因此它与标准差、极差等概念搭配。

senses.title: Biological Variation
senses.titleCN: 生物变异：同种个体间的差异
senses.definition: the range of differences among individuals of a species
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种个体之间的差异范围
senses.example: Genetic variability gives a population a chance to survive a new disease.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传变异让一个种群有机会熬过新的疾病。
senses.why: Evolution depends on differences, not on uniformity. Here variability is a resource: the wider the spread, the more likely some member fits a changed world.
senses.whyCN: 演化依赖差异而非整齐划一。此时 variability 是一种资源：分布越宽，越可能有某个成员适应改变了的世界。

senses.title: Climate Fluctuation
senses.definition: the degree to which climate conditions differ from year to year or place to place
senses.definitionCN: 气候条件在年际或地点之间的差异程度
senses.example: Natural variability hides the slower trend for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 自然波动会在数十年里掩盖较慢的趋势。
senses.why: A trend is a direction; variability is the noise around it. Climate science separates the two, because a wet year says nothing about a warming century.
senses.whyCN: 趋势是方向，变率是围绕方向的噪声。气候科学要把两者分开，因为一个多雨的年份说明不了整个世纪在变暖。

senses.title: Measurement Noise
senses.titleCN: 测量波动：同一对象反复测出的差别
senses.definition: the differences between repeated measurements of the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 对同一对象反复测量所得结果之间的差异
senses.example: The variability between the three readings came from the old balance.
senses.exampleCN: 三次读数的波动来自那台旧天平。
senses.why: Instruments never repeat perfectly. The noun names that scatter, and a low value is a sign of a trustworthy method rather than of a stable world.
senses.whyCN: 仪器从不完美重复；这个名词命名的正是那种分散，而数值低说明方法可信，并不说明世界稳定。

senses.title: Beat-to-Beat Range
senses.titleCN: 心率变异性：逐次心跳的间隔差
senses.definition: the variation in the time between heartbeats
senses.definitionCN: 心跳之间时间间隔的变化
senses.example: High heart rate variability is usually a sign of a healthy nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 较高的心率变异性通常意味着神经系统健康。
senses.why: Medicine uses the statistical sense on a living signal. A perfectly regular pulse can be a warning, so variability here is not noise but information.
senses.whyCN: 医学把统计义用在活体信号上；完全规律的脉搏反而可能是警讯，因此这里的变异性不是噪声，而是信息。

senses.title: Genetic Range
senses.titleCN: 遗传变异度：基因库里的多样性
senses.definition: the amount of genetic difference carried within a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体内部所携带的遗传差异总量
senses.example: The island population lost much of its genetic variability.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛屿种群失去了大部分遗传变异。
senses.why: Small populations lose variants by chance. The word then measures a store of options, which conservation biology treats as something to protect.
senses.whyCN: 小种群会因偶然丢失变体；此时这个词量的是选项的储备，保护生物学把它当作需要保护的对象。

senses.title: Inconsistency of Quality
senses.definition: the unevenness of quality or performance over time
senses.definitionCN: 质量或表现在时间上的不均衡
senses.example: Customers complained about the variability of the product.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客抱怨该产品的质量波动。
senses.why: In manufacturing, variability is the enemy of trust: two units of the same model should behave alike. The word shifts from description to a defect to be reduced.
senses.whyCN: 在制造业，变异性是信任的敌人：同一型号的两件产品应当表现一致。此时该词从描述变成一种应当被降低的缺陷。

intro.en: Variability is formed from variable plus -ity, and variable comes from Latin variabilis, from variare 'to change', from varius 'diverse, spotted'. The origin of varius itself is uncertain, and the first English date is only approximate.
intro.cn: variability 由 variable 加 -ity 构成；variable 出自拉丁 variabilis，来自 variare「变化」，而 variare 又来自 varius「多样的、有斑点的」。varius 本身的来源不确定，英语首见年代仅为约数。

items.en: Varius meant 'of various kinds, spotted, mottled, changeable'. Its deeper origin is uncertain: some connect it with a root for 'to weave or vary', but no source is agreed.
items.cn: varius 意为「多种多样的、有斑点的、斑驳的、易变的」。它更深的来源不确定：有人把它与表示「编织、变化」的词根联系起来，但没有公认的来源。此处标注为来源不确定。

items.en: The verb variare meant 'to diversify, to change, to alternate'. It was used for colouring, for altering a plan and for taking turns.
items.cn: 动词 variare 意为「使多样、改变、交替」，可用于上色、改变计划，也可指轮流。

items.en: Variabilis meant 'changeable, inconstant'. Latin built it with the suffix -bilis, 'able to be', which English keeps in -able.
items.cn: variabilis 意为「可变的、不恒定的」。拉丁语用后缀 -bilis「能够被……」构成它，英语以 -able 保留了这个后缀。

items.en: English variable appears in the fifteenth century from Old French. Variability followed later, adding -ity to make the quality into a noun. Exact first citations are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 variable 于十五世纪经古法语出现；variability 稍后加上 -ity，把这种性质变成名词。确切的首见书证不确定。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries variability acquired a technical sense in statistics and biology: the measurable spread of a set of observations. The old idea of changeability became a number.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，variability 在统计学与生物学中获得专门含义：一组观测值可测量的离散程度。古老的「易变」观念由此变成了一个数字。

note.en: The first group separates nouns and adjectives of the same Latin family that are easy to mix. The second holds near-synonyms from statistics and everyday speech.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的名词与形容词；第二组是统计学与日常用语中的近义词。

entries.definition: A particular change or difference, or the act of varying. It counts differences; variability measures how large the differences are.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一具体变化或差异，或变化的行为；它数差异的个数，而 variability 量差异的大小。

entries.definition: In statistics, the average squared deviation; in law, a permission to depart from a rule. It is a precise quantity, not a general quality.
entries.definitionCN: 统计学中指离差平方的平均值；法律中指对规则适用的例外许可。它是精确的量，不是一般的性质。

entries.definition: The adjective 'changeable' or the noun for a quantity that can take different values. The noun names the thing that varies, not the amount of varying.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「易变的」，或指可取不同值的量；该名词命名的是会变的东西，而不是变化的幅度。

entries.definition: An irregular rising and falling, as of prices. It stresses movement up and down rather than the spread of values.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则地上下起伏，如价格；强调上下运动，而不是数值的分散。

entries.definition: A tendency to change or become unbalanced. It carries more risk and less measurement than variability.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于变化或失衡；比 variability 含更多风险意味，更少测量意味。

entries.definition: The presence of many different kinds. It counts variety of types, while variability measures differences within a measure.
entries.definitionCN: 存在许多不同种类；它数类型的多样，而 variability 量同一度量内的差异。

entries.definition: The spreading of values around a centre. It is a technical near-synonym of variability in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 数值围绕中心散布；在统计学中是 variability 的技术性近义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: varius 'varied' + -able 'able to' + -ity: the quality of being able to vary.
normal.cn: varius「多样的」+ -able「能够」+ -ity：能够变化的性质。

normal.en: The family runs vary, variable, variability, variation, variance, variant, various.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 vary、variable、variability、variation、variance、variant、various。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: climate variability, genetic variability, heart rate variability, measurement variability.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：气候变率、遗传变异度、心率变异性、测量波动。

normal.en: variability is how much things differ; variation is a particular difference.
normal.cn: variability 是差异有多大，variation 是某一处具体的差异。

normal.en: Low variability in a factory is good; high variability in a gene pool is good.
normal.cn: 工厂里变异性低是好事，基因库里变异性高是好事。

abstract.en: Picture a row of ten identical cups, then a row where every cup is a different height.
abstract.cn: 想象一排十只一模一样的杯子，再想象一排每只高度都不同的杯子。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across a scatter of dots to show how far they wander from the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺横放在散乱的点上，用来显示它们离中心有多远。

abstract.en: Picture a heartbeat that is never exactly on time, and a doctor smiling at the irregularity.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗从不准时的心跳，而医生对这种不规则微笑。

examples.en: The study measured the variability of response times across four groups.
examples.cn: 该研究测量了四组反应时间的波动程度。

examples.en: High variability in rainfall forces farmers to store water.
examples.cn: 降水的剧烈变动迫使农民储水。

examples.en: Reducing variability is the first aim of any production line.
examples.cn: 降低波动是任何生产线的首要目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: variable（可变的）+ ility（性质）→ 可变的程度 → 可变性、变异性

root: 拉丁 varius「多样的、有斑点的」（来源不确定）→ variare「变化」→ variabilis「可变的」→ 英语 variable → variability。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure how much something differs: a general quality, a statistical spread, biological difference, climate noise, instrument scatter, heartbeat range, genetic variety and uneven quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量「差异有多大」：一般性质、统计离散、生物差异、气候噪声、仪器散布、心跳间隔、遗传多样与质量起伏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of unequal harvests, and a ruler laid across the differences.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排高低不等的收成，一把尺子横放在这些差异之上。

branches.en: QUALITY BECOMES QUANTITY: a vague property of being changeable turns into a measurable spread.
branches.cn: 性质变成数量：模糊的「易变」性质变成了可测量的离散度。

branches.en: VARIATION AS RESOURCE: genetic differences give a population options, and a narrow pool is a risk.
branches.cn: 变异作为资源：遗传差异给种群提供选项，而狭窄的基因库是一种风险。

branches.en: NOISE VERSUS TREND: year-to-year wobble can hide a slow direction for decades.
branches.cn: 噪声与趋势：年际抖动可以在数十年里掩盖缓慢的方向。

branches.en: READING A SIGNAL: in instruments the scatter means error, while in a heartbeat it can mean health.
branches.cn: 读取信号：在仪器上散布意味着误差，在心跳上却可能意味着健康。

branches.en: QUALITY CONTROL: identical products should behave alike, so variability becomes a defect to reduce.
branches.cn: 质量控制：相同产品应当表现一致，因此变异性成为需要降低的缺陷。

intro.en: Variability is a Latin-rooted adjective turned into a quality-noun: a root meaning 'varied', the suffix -able, and the suffix -ity.
intro.cn: variability 是拉丁词根的形容词转化为性质名词：表示「多样」的词根、后缀 -able，以及后缀 -ity。

latinIntro.en: Latin varius and variare supply vary, variable, variability, variation, variance, variant, various and varietas, the ancestor of variety.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 varius 与 variare 衍生 vary、variable、variability、variation、variance、variant、various，以及 variety 的祖形 varietas。

items.example: Variability in the data was greater than expected.
items.exampleCN: 数据的波动比预期更大。

items.meaning: changeable; a quantity that can vary
items.meaningCN: 易变的；可取不同值的量
items.example: Temperature is the key variable in the experiment.
items.exampleCN: 温度是该实验的关键变量。

items.example: Results vary widely between regions.
items.exampleCN: 各地结果差异很大。

items.meaning: a change; a difference in form
items.example: Slight variation in colour is normal.
items.exampleCN: 颜色的轻微差异是正常的。

items.meaningCN: 差异；离差平方的平均值
items.example: The variance of the sample was small.
items.exampleCN: 样本的方差很小。

items.meaning: a different form of the same thing
items.example: A rare variant appeared in the north.
items.exampleCN: 北方出现了一种罕见的变体。

items.example: The shelf held various tools.
items.exampleCN: 架子上放着各种工具。

items.example: The garden grows a wide variety of herbs.
items.exampleCN: 园子里种着多种香草。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 多样的；有斑点的；易变的（更深来源不确定）

definition_zh: 文化多样性；多种文化并存的状态；不同文化表达方式的丰富差异；（政策、教育中的）文化多元原则
definition_en: the existence of many different cultures and cultural expressions in one place or in the world
core_image: 一张社区地图上标满了不同语言的住户，每一种颜色都代表一种在家中使用的话
scene: 社区调查员挨家挨户问在家里说哪种语言，再把结果一格一格填进表格， The report measures cultural diversity by counting languages spoken at home.
sceneCN: 这里 cultural diversity 指「可以用数量衡量的文化差异程度」（第 4 个义项：可测量的文化多样性）；句意为报告通过统计家庭中使用的语言来衡量文化多样性。图中可辨识物件：社区地图、语言标签、统计表格、调查员的笔。

pos.zh: 文化多样性；多种文化并存；文化表达的丰富差异

forms.label: 复数（多种文化多样性情形）

senses.title: Many cultures existing in one society
senses.titleCN: 同一社会中存在多种文化
senses.definition: the presence of several distinct cultures within one society or place
senses.definitionCN: 同一社会或地点内存在多种不同文化
senses.example: Cultural diversity is visible in the market, where five languages share one counter.
senses.exampleCN: 文化多样性在市场上就能看见：五种语言共用同一个柜台。
senses.why: The phrase joins a cultural adjective to a noun of difference: what varies is not goods or genes but ways of life.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把「文化的」形容词与表示差异的名词连在一起：变化的不是货物或基因，而是生活方式。

senses.title: The variety of cultural expressions worldwide
senses.titleCN: 全世界文化表达的丰富差异
senses.definition: the range of languages, arts, rituals and customs found across the world
senses.definitionCN: 世界各地语言、艺术、仪式与习俗的丰富范围
senses.example: The atlas records cultural diversity in songs, scripts and seasonal feasts.
senses.exampleCN: 这本图集记录歌曲、文字与节令宴飨中的文化多样性。
senses.why: The phrase can widen from one society to the whole planet, where diversity means the total stock of human variety.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以从一个社会扩展到整个星球，此时多样性指人类全部变异的库存。

senses.title: A policy principle and public value
senses.definition: the principle that cultural variety should be protected and supported by public policy
senses.definitionCN: 文化差异应受公共政策保护与支持的 principle
senses.example: The convention treats cultural diversity as a common heritage of humanity.
senses.exampleCN: 该公约把文化多样性视为人类的共同遗产。
senses.why: Once diversity is declared a good, the phrase moves from description to obligation: variety must be defended, not merely observed.
senses.whyCN: 一旦多样性被宣布为善，这个短语就从描述转为义务：差异必须被捍卫，而不只是被观察。

senses.title: A measurable variety
senses.definition: a quantity that can be counted or indexed, such as the number of languages or cultural groups in a place
senses.definitionCN: 可以用计数或指数衡量的量，如某地语言或文化群体的数量
senses.example: The report measures cultural diversity by counting languages spoken at home.
senses.exampleCN: 报告通过统计家庭中使用的语言来衡量文化多样性。
senses.why: Policy and research need numbers, so the phrase also names a variable that can be counted, compared and mapped.
senses.whyCN: 政策与研究需要数字，因此这个短语也命名一个可以计数、比较与绘图的变量。

senses.title: An educational principle
senses.definition: the principle that teaching should reflect and explain several cultural traditions
senses.definitionCN: 教学应反映并解释多种文化传统的原则
senses.example: Cultural diversity in the curriculum means more than adding one festival to the calendar.
senses.exampleCN: 课程中的文化多样性不只是往日历上加一个节日。
senses.why: Schools decide which inheritance is passed on, so the phrase becomes a demand about what students will read and celebrate.
senses.whyCN: 学校决定传递哪一份遗产，因此这个短语变成关于学生读什么、庆祝什么的主张。

senses.title: Variety inside an organization
senses.definition: the mix of cultural backgrounds among employees, members or students in one institution
senses.definitionCN: 一个机构内员工、成员或学生文化背景的混合
senses.example: The hospital's cultural diversity shows in its interpreters and its kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院的文化多样性体现在口译员与厨房里。
senses.why: Institutions count diversity for practical reasons: different backgrounds bring different needs, skills and blind spots.
senses.whyCN: 机构出于实际理由统计多样性：不同背景带来不同需求、技能与盲点。

senses.title: A field of study
senses.definition: the academic study of how cultural variety is produced, maintained and governed
senses.definitionCN: 研究文化差异如何产生、维持与治理的学术领域
senses.example: Cultural diversity is now a subject with its own journals and methods.
senses.exampleCN: 文化多样性如今是一个有自己的期刊与方法的研究领域。
senses.why: The phrase can name a discipline, not its object: scholars study diversity itself, including the ways it is counted.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以指一门学科，而不只是它的对象：学者研究多样性本身，包括它被计数的方式。

senses.title: Variety represented in art and media
senses.titleCN: 艺术与媒体中呈现的多样性
senses.definition: the representation of several cultures in films, exhibitions, broadcasts or literature
senses.definitionCN: 在电影、展览、广播或文学中呈现多种文化
senses.example: The festival's cultural diversity is real only if the smaller communities also perform.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当较小的社群也登台，这个节庆的文化多样性才是真实的。
senses.why: Representation is where diversity becomes visible: a screen or a stage can either show the many cultures or flatten them into one.
senses.whyCN: 呈现是多样性变得可见之处：屏幕或舞台既可以展示多种文化，也可以把它们压成一种。

intro.en: Cultural diversity joins cultural, from Latin cultura, with diversity, from Latin diversitas and divertere, to turn apart. The phrase is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultural diversity 由 cultural 与 diversity 结合而成；cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura，diversity 来自拉丁语 diversitas 与 divertere「转向不同方向」。这是个现代短语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn. With the prefix dis-, apart, it gave divertere, to turn aside or turn in different directions.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转动」。加上表示「分开」的前缀 dis-，构成 divertere「转向一边、转向不同方向」。

items.en: The past participle diversus meant turned apart, hence different or varied; English diverse comes from it.
items.cn: 过去分词 diversus 意为「被转向不同方向的」，因此表示「不同的、多样的」；英语 diverse 由此而来。

items.en: Diversitas named difference and variety, and English diversity was borrowed through French.
items.cn: diversitas 指差异与多样，英语 diversity 经法语借入。

items.en: Cultura, tilling and care, gave English culture and cultural; in this phrase culture means the learned way of life.
items.cn: cultura 意为耕作与照料，给出英语 culture 与 cultural；在这个短语里，culture 指习得的生活方式。

items.en: Cultural diversity became a policy phrase in the late twentieth century, and the UNESCO convention of two thousand and five fixed it in international law.
items.cn: cultural diversity 在二十世纪后期成为政策短语，二〇〇五年的联合国教科文组织公约把它写进国际法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the phrase is not securely dated, and the pre-Latin origin of vertere remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个短语在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；vertere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same diversity stock or its biological parallel; the second holds terms for plural societies and variety.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 diversity 词干或与之并行的生物学术语；第二组是关于多元社会与差异的术语。

entries.definition: The variety of living species and ecosystems; it borrows the diversity noun but counts organisms, not cultures.
entries.definitionCN: 生物物种与生态系统的多样性；它借用了 diversity 这个名词，但数的是生物，不是文化。

entries.definition: Variety in general; cultural diversity specifies that the variety is in cultures rather than in genes or products.
entries.definitionCN: 一般意义上的多样性；cultural diversity 指明差异在文化上，而非基因或产品上。

entries.definition: Showing much variety; the phrase cultural diversity needs the noun, while diverse can describe anything.
entries.definitionCN: 显示出丰富差异；短语 cultural diversity 需要名词，而 diverse 可描述任何事物。

entries.definition: The process of adding more kinds or types; it names an action, while cultural diversity names a state.
entries.definitionCN: 增加更多种类或类型的过程；它指动作，而 cultural diversity 指状态。

entries.definition: The policy or ideology that supports several cultures; cultural diversity can be the fact that the doctrine responds to.
entries.definitionCN: 支持多种文化的政策或意识形态；cultural diversity 可以指这套主张所回应的事实。

entries.definition: Acceptance of many groups or viewpoints; broader than cultural diversity, which focuses on culture.
entries.definitionCN: 接受多个群体或观点；比聚焦文化的 cultural diversity 更宽。

entries.definition: The quality of being made of unlike parts; it is a neutral technical term, while cultural diversity often carries a value.
entries.definitionCN: 由不同部分构成的性质；它是中性的技术术语，而 cultural diversity 常带价值判断。

entries.definition: The presence of many kinds of a thing; it is wider and less political than cultural diversity.
entries.definitionCN: 同一种事物有许多种类；它比 cultural diversity 更宽、更少政治含义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real roots of both words and the phrases the term actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个词的真实词根，以及这个术语实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: cultural means of culture, and diversity means turned apart, so the phrase names ways of life that have turned in different directions.
normal.cn: cultural 表示「文化的」，diversity 表示「被转向不同方向的」，所以这个短语指转向不同方向的各种生活方式。

normal.en: The family runs diverse, diversity, diversify, diversification and biodiversity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 diverse（多样的）、diversity（多样性）、diversify（使多样化）、diversification（多样化）、biodiversity（生物多样性）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: preserve cultural diversity, cultural diversity policy, cultural diversity index.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：保护文化多样性、文化多样性政策、文化多样性指数。

normal.en: The word became a policy term when international bodies began protecting cultural variety.
normal.cn: 当国际机构开始保护文化差异时，这个词成为政策术语。

normal.en: Its biological twin is biodiversity; both count variety, but one counts cultures and the other counts species.
normal.cn: 它在生物学上的对应词是 biodiversity（生物多样性）；两者都数多样性，但一个数文化，一个数物种。

abstract.en: Picture a map coloured by language rather than by border.
abstract.cn: 想象一张按语言而不是按国界上色的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of instruments, each tuned to a different scale, all playable in one room.
abstract.cn: 想象一架乐器，每件都调在不同的音阶上，却都能在同一间屋里演奏。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe book where no page repeats the same spice.
abstract.cn: 想象一本菜谱，没有一页重复同一种香料。

examples.en: Cultural diversity is protected by law in some countries and ignored in others.
examples.cn: 文化多样性在一些国家受法律保护，在另一些国家则被忽视。

examples.en: The museum's programme celebrates cultural diversity without turning it into a spectacle.
examples.cn: 博物馆的项目颂扬文化多样性，却没有把它变成一场奇观。

examples.en: Measuring cultural diversity by language alone misses shared customs that cross languages.
examples.cn: 只按语言衡量文化多样性，会漏掉跨语言共有的习俗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「文化的」加「多样性」——许多种文化并存，就是文化多样性。

root: 由 cultural 与 diversity 组成。cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」，再往前是 colere「耕种、敬拜」；diversity 来自拉丁语 diversitas，而 diversitas 出自动词 divertere「转向不同方向」，由 dis-「分开」与 vertere「转动」构成。colere 与 vertere 的更早来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one variety: a society, the world, a policy, a number, a classroom, a workplace, a discipline and finally a stage or screen.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种「差异」展开：一个社会、整个世界、一项政策、一个数字、一间教室、一个职场、一门学科，最后是一块舞台或屏幕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map in which every colour is a language and no colour covers the whole page.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张地图，每种颜色都是一种语言，没有一种颜色盖满整页。

branches.en: LOCAL AND GLOBAL: the same variety can be seen inside one market or across the whole planet.
branches.cn: 本地与全球：同一种差异既可以在一个市场里看见，也可以在整个星球上看见。

branches.en: PUBLIC VALUE: variety becomes something a society is obliged to protect.
branches.cn: 公共价值：差异变成社会有义务保护的东西。

branches.en: INDEX: the variety is turned into a number that can be compared and mapped.
branches.cn: 指数：差异被转化为可以比较与绘图的数字。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: schools and workplaces must both reflect the variety they serve.
branches.cn: 机构：学校与职场都必须反映它们所服务的多样性。

branches.en: STUDY AND SCREEN: diversity becomes a discipline, and representation becomes the test of whether it is real.
branches.cn: 研究与屏幕：多样性成为一门学科，而呈现则成为检验它是否真实的标准。

intro.en: Cultural diversity is two Latin-derived words joined: a culture adjective and a noun of turning apart.
intro.cn: cultural diversity 是两个源自拉丁语的词组合而成：一个文化形容词与一个表示「转向不同方向」的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cultura and -alis give cultural; dis- plus vertere give diversus, diversitas and English diversity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cultura 与 -alis 给出 cultural；dis- 加 vertere 给出 diversus、diversitas 与英语 diversity。

items.example: The verb also builds convert and reverse.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也构成 convert（转变）与 reverse（反转）。

items.structure: dis- (Latin prefix, apart, in different directions)
items.example: The prefix turns turning into turning apart.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「转动」变成「转向不同方向」。

items.meaningCN: 被转向不同方向的；不同的
items.example: The participle gave English diverse.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词给出英语 diverse。

items.example: The noun became English diversity through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经法语成为英语 diversity。

items.example: The noun became English culture through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经法语成为英语 culture。

items.example: The ending builds cultural and natural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 cultural（文化的）与 natural（自然的）。

items.example: The forest is known for its diversity.
items.exampleCN: 这片森林以多样性著称。

items.example: The farm diversified into fruit.
items.exampleCN: 这个农场多样化经营，种起了水果。

items.example: The city has a cultural programme.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市有一项文化项目。

latinEntries.structure: vertere, verti, versum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
diversus, diversa, diversum (Latin participle and adjective)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 转向不同方向的；不同的

definition_zh: 假设；提出假说；假定（以便检验或推理）
definition_en: to propose a tentative explanation that can be tested, or to assume something for the sake of argument
core_image: 白板中央写着一个尚未验证的猜测，旁边画出一条通向可测结果的箭头
scene: 讨论会上，研究者在白板中央写下一条还没验证的解释，再画出检验它的步骤。 They hypothesize that the mould grows faster in damp air.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：提出一个尚待检验的解释；句意为他们假定霉菌在潮湿空气中长得更快。图中可辨识物件：白板、箭头、问号、记录贴。

pos.zh: 假设；提出假说；假定（可及物或接从句）

senses.title: To propose a testable explanation
senses.definition: to put forward an explanation that further observation or experiment can support or contradict
senses.definitionCN: 提出一种能由后续观察或实验支持或否定的解释
senses.example: They hypothesize that the mould grows faster in damp air.
senses.exampleCN: 他们假定霉菌在潮湿空气中长得更快。
senses.why: A hypothesis is a placing under, a foundation laid down so that a test can stand on it, which is why the verb needs something checkable.
senses.whyCN: 假说字面上是垫在下面的基座，先铺好基础，检验才能站上去，因此这个动词要求的正是可被检验的内容。

senses.title: To assume for an argument
senses.definition: to take something as true temporarily in order to work out what would follow
senses.definitionCN: 为推出后续结论而暂时把某事当作真的
senses.example: Let us hypothesize a world without friction and see what fails.
senses.exampleCN: 让我们假定一个没有摩擦的世界，看看什么会失灵。
senses.why: In a proof or a debate, a supposition is a working floor rather than a claim about reality.
senses.whyCN: 在证明或辩论里，假定只是临时地板，并非关于现实的主张。

senses.title: To guess without much evidence
senses.definition: to offer a guess about a cause or a possibility, often in ordinary conversation
senses.definitionCN: 对成因或可能性给出猜测，常用于日常谈话
senses.example: He hypothesized about the noise but never checked the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那阵响声作了猜测，却从没上屋顶查看。
senses.why: The scientific word keeps a weaker everyday use, where the guess is not yet tied to a test.
senses.whyCN: 这个科学词保留了较弱的日常用法，此时猜测尚未与检验挂钩。

senses.title: To predict a specific outcome
senses.definition: to state in advance what a model or theory implies should happen in a given case
senses.definitionCN: 预先说明模型或理论在特定情形下应当产生什么结果
senses.example: The team hypothesized a rise of two degrees and set the sensor to catch it.
senses.exampleCN: 团队预测会上升两度，并设好传感器去捕捉它。
senses.why: Once a model is written, its next case is a prediction, and the verb marks the step from model to expected number.
senses.whyCN: 模型写成之后，下一个情形就是预测，这个动词标出从模型到预期数字的一步。

senses.title: To state a statistical relation
senses.titleCN: 在统计中假定某种关系
senses.definition: to frame a relation between variables as a hypothesis to be tested against data
senses.definitionCN: 把变量之间的关系表述成待用数据检验的假说
senses.example: We hypothesize a link between sleep and recall.
senses.exampleCN: 我们假定睡眠与回忆之间存在联系。
senses.why: Statistics needs a statement precise enough to be rejected, and the verb supplies that statement.
senses.whyCN: 统计学需要一个精确到能被否定的陈述，这个动词提供的就是那个陈述。

senses.title: To reconstruct a possible past
senses.definition: to propose what may have happened in the past from the traces that remain
senses.definitionCN: 根据残留痕迹提出过去可能发生了什么
senses.example: Historians hypothesize a trading post beneath the car park.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学者假定停车场下面曾有一个贸易站。
senses.why: When no document survives, the past can only be rebuilt as supposition, and the word fits that limit.
senses.whyCN: 没有文件留存时，过去只能作为假定重建，这个词正好承认这一限制。

senses.title: To posit something unseen
senses.definition: to propose the existence of an entity that has not yet been detected, because a theory requires it
senses.definitionCN: 因理论需要而提出某物的存在，尽管尚未探测到
senses.example: Physicists hypothesized a particle that no detector had yet found.
senses.exampleCN: 物理学家假定了一种尚无探测器找到的粒子。
senses.why: A theory can demand a missing piece, and naming it in advance is how the search is organised.
senses.whyCN: 理论可能需要一块缺失的拼图，提前给它命名正是组织搜寻的方式。

senses.title: To ask learners to predict
senses.definition: in teaching, to ask students to state what they expect before they observe or test
senses.definitionCN: 在教学中让学生先说出预期，再去观察或检验
senses.example: The teacher asked the class to hypothesize before adding the acid.
senses.exampleCN: 老师让全班在加酸之前先作假设。
senses.why: A prediction made before the demonstration gives the learner a stake in the result.
senses.whyCN: 在演示之前先作预测，能让学习者与结果产生切身关系。

senses.title: To form a working guess in practice
senses.titleCN: 在实践中先立一个可用的猜测
senses.definition: to adopt a provisional explanation while solving a practical problem, ready to drop it if it fails
senses.definitionCN: 在解决实际问题时先采用一个临时解释，一旦失败就放弃
senses.example: The mechanic hypothesized a blocked filter and tested it first.
senses.exampleCN: 修车工先假定滤芯堵塞，并优先验证这一点。
senses.why: A working guess saves time by directing the next test, even before any formal study exists.
senses.whyCN: 可用的猜测通过指明下一步测试来省时间，即使还没有正式研究。

intro.en: Hypothesize is an English verb built on hypothesis, from Greek hypothesis 'a placing under, a foundation'. The Greeks used it for a geometric base, and the modern sense of a testable supposition grew from that.
intro.cn: hypothesize 是在名词 hypothesis 上加动词词尾构成的英语动词；hypothesis 来自希腊语，意为「垫在下面、基座」。希腊人用它指几何中的基础，现代「可检验的假定」这一义正是从那里长出来的。

items.en: The prefix meant under or beneath, the same element that gives hypodermic and a hypothesis laid under a claim.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为在下面，与「皮下」一词同源；假说就是垫在主张下面的东西。

items.en: Thesis meant a placing or setting down, from tithenai 'to put', the verb behind theme and thesis.
items.cn: thesis 意为放置、放下，出自 tithenai「放」，也是 theme 与 thesis 的词根。

items.en: In geometry a hypothesis was the base or assumption on which a proof stood; in ordinary speech it was a supposition.
items.cn: 在几何里，假说是证明所站立的基座或前提；在日常说法里，它是一个假定。

items.en: Latin took hypothesis as a term of logic, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁语把假说作为逻辑术语接收，英语在十六世纪将其借入。

items.en: English formed hypothesize on the noun with the productive ending -ize; the verb is recorded from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语用能产的词尾 -ize 在名词上造出这个动词，十七世纪已有记录。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the verb settled into the method of stating a testable prediction before measuring.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，这个动词固定为「先陈述可检验的预测、再测量」的方法步骤。

note.en: The first group shares the hypothesis stem, with one false friend; the second group names weaker or stronger ways of positing.
note.cn: 第一组共享「假说」词干，其中有一个假朋友；第二组是程度不同的设定方式。

entries.definition: The noun: a testable explanation, plural hypotheses with the Greek -es ending.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：可检验的解释，复数保留希腊式词尾。

entries.definition: The adjective: supposed rather than established.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：属于假定而非已确立的。

entries.definition: The adverb: in a supposed case, not in fact.
entries.definitionCN: 副词：在假定情形下，而非事实中。

entries.definition: To pledge property as security; from a Greek word for a pledge, not a supposition.
entries.definitionCN: 以财产作抵押担保；出自希腊语中表示抵押的词，与假定无关。

entries.definition: A person who proposes hypotheses, a rare but regular agent noun.
entries.definitionCN: 提出假说的人，罕见但合乎构词规则。

entries.definition: To reason from incomplete evidence, with less commitment to testing.
entries.definitionCN: 凭不完整证据推理，对检验的承诺更弱。

entries.definition: To take something as a starting principle without deriving it.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事当作出发点，而不加推导。

entries.definition: To form an opinion on thin evidence; the noun is commoner than the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 凭薄弱证据形成看法；名词比动词更常用。

entries.definition: The everyday word for taking something as true for now.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指暂时把某事当作真的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek 'placing under', the real family and the fixed frames of research writing.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用希腊语「垫在下面」这一构词意象、真实同族词，以及科研写作里的固定框架。

normal.en: Greek hypothesis was a base laid under a proof, and a testable guess is still a floor to stand on.
normal.cn: 希腊语中的假说是铺在证明下面的基座，可检验的猜测至今仍是站立的地板。

normal.en: The family runs hypothesis, hypothesize, hypothetical, hypothetically and hypothesizer.
normal.cn: 同族词有 hypothesis、hypothesize、hypothetical、hypothetically 与 hypothesizer。

normal.en: Research writing fixes the frame: hypothesize that, hypothesize a relationship, test a hypothesized link.
normal.cn: 科研写作有固定框架：假定……、假定某种关系、检验假定的联系。

normal.en: The plural of the noun is hypotheses, keeping the Greek ending.
normal.cn: 名词复数是 hypotheses，保留了希腊语词尾。

normal.en: Hypothecate looks identical in front but means to pledge property, not to suppose.
normal.cn: hypothecate 前半截相同，意思却是抵押财产，而非假定。

abstract.en: To hypothesize is to build a floor you are willing to remove.
abstract.cn: 提出假说，就是搭一层你愿意拆掉的地板。

abstract.en: A guess becomes a hypothesis only when it says what would count against it.
abstract.cn: 猜测只有在说清什么能反驳它时，才成为假说。

abstract.en: The sentence that can be tested is worth more than the sentence that sounds certain.
abstract.cn: 能被检验的句子，比听起来肯定的句子更有价值。

examples.en: The team hypothesized that the two groups would differ by one grade.
examples.cn: 团队假定两组会相差一个等级。

examples.en: It is easy to hypothesize a cause and hard to rule one out.
examples.cn: 假定一个成因很容易，排除一个却很难。

examples.en: She hypothesized a second pathway before the first was mapped.
examples.cn: 在第一条路径被画出之前，她就假定存在第二条。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「海剖塞赛兹」——先抛出一个猜想，再剖开来看真假：假设

root: 希腊语 hypo「在下」+ thesis「放置」→ hypothesis「垫在下面的基座、假定」；英语加 -ize 造出动词。其后缀化的 -ize 来自希腊语构词习惯，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one laid-down foundation: a testable explanation, a temporary assumption, a loose guess, a predicted outcome, a statistical relation, a rebuilt past, an unseen entity, a classroom prediction and a working guess in a workshop.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一块铺下的基座：可检验的解释、临时的假定、随口猜测、预测结果、统计关系、重建的过去、看不见的实体、课堂上的预测，以及车间里的临时猜测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a guess is written in the middle of the board with an arrow drawn to the test that could break it.
core.cn: 核心意象：白板中央写下一个猜测，旁边画一支指向能推翻它的检验的箭头。

branches.en: THE TESTABLE CLAIM: an explanation and a stated relation, both precise enough to fail.
branches.cn: 可检验的主张：一个解释与一个关系陈述，两者都精确到可以失败。

branches.en: THE SUPPOSITION: a floor for argument, or a guess not yet tied to any test.
branches.cn: 假定：或为推理铺地板，或只是尚未与检验挂钩的猜测。

branches.en: THE PREDICTION: a number expected from a model, or a class asked to commit before the demo.
branches.cn: 预测：模型给出的预期数字，或让全班在演示前先下注。

branches.en: THE UNSEEN: a past rebuilt from traces, an entity named before it is found.
branches.cn: 看不见的东西：由痕迹重建的过去，与被找到之前先命名的实体。

branches.en: THE WORKING GUESS: a provisional cause adopted to decide which test comes first.
branches.cn: 临时猜测：先采用一个成因，用来决定先做哪项测试。

intro.en: Hypothesize joins a Greek compound noun to the productive verb ending -ize; the pieces are hypo, thesis and tithenai.
intro.cn: hypothesize 把希腊语复合名词与能产的动词词尾 -ize 接在一起，部件是 hypo、thesis 与 tithenai。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek in origin and reached English through Latin; the Latin layer here is the borrowed noun hypothesis and the ending -izare.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自希腊语，经拉丁语进入英语；此处的拉丁语成分是借入的名词 hypothesis 与词尾 -izare。

items.example: The verb is English, the noun is Greek.
items.exampleCN: 动词是英语造的，名词来自希腊语。

items.example: It marks the base laid under a claim.
items.exampleCN: 它标出铺在主张下面的基座。

items.example: The noun names the act of putting something in place.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名把某物放到位的动作。

items.example: The verb is the far root of both thesis and theme.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是「放置」与「主题」两词的远根。

items.example: Geometry gave the word its first technical home.
items.exampleCN: 几何学给了这个词第一个专业归宿。

items.example: The ending turns nouns into verbs across English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾在英语里把名词变成动词。

items.example: The adjective marks the status of the claim.
items.exampleCN: 形容词标出主张的地位。

items.example: The adverb sets the whole sentence in a supposition.
items.exampleCN: 副词把整句放进一个假定里。

items.example: It shares the prefix but not the supposition.
items.exampleCN: 它共享前缀，却没有「假定」之义。

latinEntries.structure: Greek hypothesis, from hypo- (under) + thesis (placing); borrowed into Latin
latinEntries.example: Latin took hypothesis from Greek with the meaning of a placed base.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语从希腊语借入 hypothesis，义为「垫在下面的基座」。

latinEntries.structure: Greek prefix hypo- (under), carried into Latin borrowings
latinEntries.example: Greek hypo- appears in Latin borrowings such as hypothesis.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 hypo- 见于 hypothesis 这类拉丁借词。

latinEntries.structure: Medieval Latin verb ending -izare, from Greek -izein
latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin -izare builds verbs such as organizare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 -izare 构成 organizare 这类动词。

latinEntries.structure: Greek thesis (a placing), from tithenai (to put)
latinEntries.example: Greek thesis means a placing, and Latin borrowed it unchanged.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 thesis 意为放置，拉丁语原样借入。

definition_zh: 充气；通气；使暴露于空气
definition_en: to introduce air into a material or substance
core_image: 园艺叉插进草坪再拔起，留下一排透气的小孔
scene: 园丁推着打孔机在草坪上来回走，泥土里冒出细孔。 They aerate the lawn each spring so the roots can breathe.
sceneCN: 这里 aerate 是「给土壤通气」（第 1 个义项：把空气引入某物）；句意为他们每年春天给草坪打孔通气，让根系得以呼吸。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「通气；充气」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「充气器；打孔机」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「充了气的」

senses.title: Introduce air into soil or material
senses.definition: to force air into soil, compost or another material
senses.definitionCN: 把空气压入土壤、堆肥或其他材料中
senses.example: They aerate the lawn each spring so the roots can breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每年春天给草坪打孔通气，让根系得以呼吸。
senses.why: Greek aer means 'air', so the verb is literally 'to put air into'.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」，所以这个动词字面上就是「把空气放进去」。

senses.title: Charge a liquid with gas
senses.definition: to add carbon dioxide or another gas to a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 往液体里加入二氧化碳或其他气体
senses.example: The bar served aerated water with strong bubbles.
senses.exampleCN: 酒吧供应气泡很足的充气水。
senses.why: Air in the first sense generalizes to any gas stirred into a liquid.
senses.whyCN: 第一义的「空气」扩展为搅入液体的任何气体。

senses.title: Expose to fresh air
senses.definition: to let fresh air move through a space or substance
senses.definitionCN: 让新鲜空气在空间或物质中流通
senses.example: Open the windows to aerate the room after painting.
senses.exampleCN: 刷完漆后开窗给房间换换气。
senses.why: Putting air in implies letting air through: the material is opened to the atmosphere.
senses.whyCN: 「放进空气」也意味着「让空气通过」：让物质向大气敞开。

intro.en: Aerate comes from Greek aer, 'air', joined to the Latin verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: aerate 由希腊语 aer（空气）加拉丁语动词尾 -ate 构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *wer- is linked to words for rising air and wind.
items.cn: 重构词根 *wer- 与表示升腾之气和风的词相关联。

items.en: Aer meant 'air, the lower atmosphere'.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、低层大气」。

items.en: Scientific Latin aeratus meant 'charged with air', coined for chemistry.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语 aeratus 意为「充了气的」，为化学而造。

items.en: English formed aerate in the eighteenth century for chemistry and brewing.
items.cn: 英语于十八世纪造出 aerate，用于化学与酿造。

items.en: The verb now spans lawns, aquariums, wines and fizzy drinks.
items.cn: 如今该动词覆盖草坪、水族箱、醒酒与气泡饮料。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the same air root; the second gathers related breathing and gas words.
note.cn: 第一组收同属「空气」词根的词；第二组收与呼吸、气体相关的词。

entries.definition: Of the air or an antenna; shares Greek aer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「空中的；天线」；同享希腊语 aer 词根。

entries.definition: Tiny particles or gas in a spray; the sol- half means 'solution'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气溶胶；喷雾」；前半同为 aer，后半 sol 意为「溶液」。

entries.definition: Requiring oxygen; built on the same air root with bios, 'life'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「需氧的」；同用 air 词根加 bios（生命）。

entries.definition: To move fresh air through a space.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「通风」，让空气在空间中流动。

entries.definition: To add oxygen to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「供氧；加氧」。

entries.definition: To charge a drink with carbon dioxide.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使充二氧化碳」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the air root and the lawn-fork scene; the abstract hooks picture bubbles and open windows.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「空气」词根与草坪打孔场景；抽象记忆点想象气泡与敞开的窗。

normal.en: Greek aer means 'air'.
normal.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」。

normal.en: Aeration is the noun, aerator the tool.
normal.cn: aeration 是名词，aerator 是工具。

normal.en: Aerated water is full of bubbles.
normal.cn: 充气水里全是气泡。

normal.en: Aerate the lawn by punching holes.
normal.cn: 给草坪打孔就是 aerate。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks it as a verb.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 标明它是动词。

abstract.en: Picture a fork lifting plugs of green turf.
abstract.cn: 想象草叉撬起一块块绿草皮。

abstract.en: Picture bubbles racing up a glass of soda.
abstract.cn: 想象气泡在一杯汽水里竞相上蹿。

abstract.en: Picture a stuffy room breathing again.
abstract.cn: 想象一间闷室重新呼吸起来。

examples.en: They aerate the lawn each spring so the roots can breathe.
examples.cn: 他们每年春天给草坪打孔通气，让根系得以呼吸。

examples.en: Aerate the wine for a few minutes before serving.
examples.cn: 上桌前先给红酒醒几分钟气。

examples.en: Fish-tank pumps aerate the water all night.
examples.cn: 鱼缸气泵整夜给水增氧。

root: 希腊语 aer（空气）→ 新拉丁语 aeratus（充气的）→ 英语 aerate；核心义是「把空气送进东西里」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from aerating soil, to charging liquids with gas, to airing out spaces.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从给土壤通气，到给液体充气，再到给空间换气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air pushed into something dense until it breathes
core.cn: 核心意象：把空气压进密实之物，让它重新呼吸

branches.en: Holes punched so roots can breathe.
branches.cn: 打好孔让根系呼吸。

branches.en: Gas stirred into water or wine.
branches.cn: 搅进水或酒里的气体。

branches.en: Windows opened to moving air.
branches.cn: 向流动空气敞开的窗。

branches.en: Both senses let stale places breathe again.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让死气之地重新吐纳。

branches.en: Fizz is this sense's everyday face.
branches.cn: 气泡水是这个义项的日常面孔。

intro.en: The word carries the Greek air root aer- with the Latin verb ending -ate, and the family gives aerial, aerosol and aerobic.
intro.cn: 这个词带着希腊语「空气」词根 aer- 与拉丁动词尾 -ate，同族词有 aerial、aerosol 与 aerobic。

latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的祖先是从希腊语 aer 到科学拉丁语 aeratus。

definition_zh: 随机的；随意的；无目的的；无规律的；偶然的；随机存取；随机数；胡乱地
definition_en: happening or chosen without a plan, purpose, or pattern, so that no one can predict which one comes next
core_image: 一匹脱缰的马不辨方向地狂奔，马蹄落处扬起的尘土没有一条直线，谁也不知道它下一步踩向哪里
scene: 这里指「随机的」。 A programmer rolls a die across the desk and says: We pick the sample at random, so no single case can skew the result.
sceneCN: 这里 random 先出现在 at random「随机地、胡乱地」（第 2 个义项：16 世纪短语“以极大的速度”引申为“不择方向”），再作「随机抽样的」（第 4 个义项）；句意：我们随机抽取样本，这样任何单个案例都无法让结果偏斜。画面里有骰子、屏幕上的数据表和一支笔。

pos.zh: 随机的；随意的；无规律的；偶然的
（计算机）随机；随意挑选的东西

collocations.zh: 随机选取；随便挑出的组合
