senses.title: No aim, no target
senses.titleCN: 无目的的：箭射出去，不瞄准任何靶子
senses.definition: made or done without a definite aim, purpose, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 没有明确目标、目的或计划而做出或进行的
senses.example: He made a random guess and happened to be right.
senses.exampleCN: 他随便猜了一下，碰巧猜对了。
senses.why: The adjective is first recorded in the 1650s as 'having no definite aim or purpose, haphazard, not sent in a special direction'. It borrows the image of a rider who has stopped steering.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最早记录于 17 世纪 50 年代，意为“没有确定目标或目的、偶然、未被送往特定方向”。它借用了骑手放开缰绳的意象。

senses.title: At random: at full gallop
senses.titleCN: 胡乱地：原意是“以极大的速度”
senses.definition: in a way that has no plan or order, as in the phrase at random
senses.definitionCN: 毫无计划或秩序地，如短语 at random
senses.example: Books were piled at random on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 书胡乱地堆在地板上。
senses.why: The phrase at random is from the 1560s and first meant 'at great speed', from the old noun randon 'impetuosity, speed'. A horse running full tilt goes wherever momentum takes it, and speed turned into carelessness.
senses.whyCN: 短语 at random 始于 16 世纪 60 年代，原意是“以极大的速度”，来自古名词 randon“冲势、猛劲”。一匹全速奔跑的马跑到哪里全凭惯性，速度就变成了漫不经心。

senses.title: Random access: jump anywhere
senses.titleCN: 随机存取：不必从头读到尾
senses.definition: a way of reading computer memory in which any location can be reached directly, without passing through the ones before it
senses.definitionCN: 一种读取计算机存储器的方式，可直接到达任一位置，无需先经过前面的位置
senses.example: RAM stands for random access memory.
senses.exampleCN: RAM 即随机存取存储器。
senses.why: Random access is recorded from 1953 for memory that need not be read sequentially. Here random does not mean 'by chance' but 'without a fixed order': the head may jump to any address at will.
senses.whyCN: random access 记录于 1953 年，指无需顺序读取的存储器。这里 random 不是“碰运气”，而是“没有固定次序”：磁头可以随意跳到任一地址。

senses.title: Random sample: every case has a chance
senses.titleCN: 随机抽样：每个个体都有同等机会被抽中
senses.definition: a group chosen so that every member of a population has an equal chance of being selected
senses.definitionCN: 这样选出的一组样本：总体中每个成员被选中的机会相等
senses.example: Researchers took a random sample of 500 households.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者随机抽取了 500 户家庭作为样本。
senses.why: Statistics needs a procedure in which no case is favoured. The word's old sense of 'not directed toward a particular target' becomes a technical guarantee: nobody's hand steers the selection.
senses.whyCN: 统计学需要一种不偏袒任何个体的程序。这个词“不被送往特定目标”的旧义变成一项技术保证：没有哪只手在引导选择。

senses.title: No pattern at all
senses.titleCN: 无规律的：看不出可复现的花样
senses.definition: lacking any recognizable pattern, order, or regular arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏可辨认的图案、次序或规则排列的
senses.example: The cracks formed a random pattern across the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 裂缝在墙上形成毫无规律的图案。
senses.why: Once 'no aim' is applied to shapes rather than actions, random means 'no pattern'. The mind looks for a rule and finds none, which is exactly what the word reports.
senses.whyCN: 一旦“无目的”从动作转用到形状，random 就表示“无规律”。头脑去找规则却找不到，这正是这个词所报告的状态。

senses.title: By chance encounter
senses.titleCN: 偶然的：两条路线碰巧交叉
senses.definition: happening by chance rather than by arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 出于偶然而非事先安排而发生的
senses.example: A random meeting in the airport changed her career.
senses.exampleCN: 机场里的一次偶然相遇改变了她的职业道路。
senses.why: The 1650s sense already contained 'haphazard'. Two independent courses crossing without a plan is the everyday picture of chance, so random slides from 'unaimed' to 'unplanned'.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 50 年代的义项已含“偶然”。两条互不相干的路线在没有计划的情况下交叉，正是偶然的日常画面，于是 random 从“无瞄准”滑向“无安排”。

senses.title: That random person
senses.titleCN: 不相干的：不知从哪儿冒出来的那个人
senses.definition: not known or not connected to the people involved; arbitrary or irrelevant, in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 不认识或与当事人无关的；任意、不相干的（非正式用法）
senses.example: Some random guy kept texting her all night.
senses.exampleCN: 一个不知从哪儿冒出来的家伙整晚给她发消息。
senses.why: Colloquial English extended 'no connection' to people: a random stranger is one with no link to your life. The 1980s college slang sense 'person who does not belong on our floor' pushed the word toward 'outsider'.
senses.whyCN: 口语英语把“没有关联”扩展到人：a random stranger 就是与你生活毫无联系的人。20 世纪 80 年代的大学俚语义“不属于我们这层楼的人”，把这个词推向“局外人”。

senses.title: Random numbers, random choices
senses.titleCN: 随机数与随机化：把偶然做成工具
senses.definition: a number or selection produced by a process that has no predictable order, used in computing and research
senses.definitionCN: 由无可预测次序的过程产生的数字或选择，用于计算与研究
senses.example: The app generates a random number between one and ten.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用生成一到十之间的随机数。
senses.why: To use chance, people built machines and algorithms that imitate it: random number, randomize, randomizer. The adjective becomes a noun modifier for the output of an artificial process.
senses.whyCN: 为了利用偶然，人们造出模仿偶然的机器与算法：random number、randomize、randomizer。这个形容词变成名词修饰语，指一个人工过程的产物。

senses.title: Random: the odd one out
senses.titleCN: 俚语里的“怪人”：不属于这里的那一个
senses.definition: in 1980s U.S. college slang, an inferior or undesirable person, especially one who does not belong
senses.definitionCN: 20 世纪 80 年代美国大学俚语中指次等或不受欢迎的人，尤指不属于此处的人
senses.example: Don't bring a random to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 别把不相干的怪人带到派对上。
senses.why: By the 1980s U.S. campus slang had turned the adjective into a noun of contempt for someone outside the group. The 'no connection' sense hardened into social exclusion.
senses.whyCN: 到 20 世纪 80 年代，美国校园俚语把这个形容词变成指称群体之外者的轻蔑名词。“没有关联”的义项硬化成了社会排斥。

intro.en: Random begins as a word for speed: a horse at full gallop has no aim. 'At great speed' became 'carelessly', then 'without plan', and finally the technical 'without fixed order' of computing.
intro.cn: random 起初是一个表示速度的词：全速奔驰的马没有目标。“极快”变成“漫不经心”，再变成“没有计划”，最后成为计算机术语里“没有固定次序”。

items.en: Frankish *rant 'a running' and Proto-Germanic *randa are reconstructed from the Old French and Germanic verbs for running. No written form survives, so this layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 法兰克语 *rant“奔跑”与原始日耳曼语 *randa 是从古法语及日耳曼语各语言的“跑”动词重构出来的。没有书面形式留存，因此这一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Randon meant 'rush, disorder, force, impetuosity', and randir 'to run fast'. The word pictures a charge rather than a stroll.
items.cn: randon 意为“冲势、混乱、力量、猛劲”，randir 意为“快跑”。这个词画的是冲锋，而不是散步。

items.en: The noun randon, randoun is recorded meaning 'impetuosity, speed'. The -n to -m spelling shift parallels seldom and ransom.
items.cn: 名词 randon、randoun 记录于约 1300 年，意为“冲势、速度”。-n 变 -m 的拼写变化与 seldom、ransom 平行。

items.en: The phrase at random appears, first meaning 'at great speed', hence 'carelessly, haphazardly'. Speed and lack of aim are fused in one idiom.
items.cn: 短语 at random 出现，最初意为“以极大的速度”，因此引申为“漫不经心、胡乱地”。速度与无目标在一个习语里熔合了。

items.en: The adjective random is recorded, 'having no definite aim or purpose, haphazard, not sent in a special direction'. The modern statistical sense grows out of this.
items.cn: 形容词 random 被记录，意为“没有确定目标或目的、偶然、未被送往特定方向”。现代统计学义即由此生长出来。

items.en: Random access is recorded in 1953 for computer memory that need not be read sequentially. By the 1980s college slang had added 'inferior, undesirable, out of place'.
items.cn: random access 记录于 1953 年，指无需顺序读取的计算机存储器。到 20 世纪 80 年代，大学俚语又添上“次等的、不受欢迎的、格格不入的”一义。

note.en: The first group shares the ran-/rand- sound and, in two cases, the actual etymology; the second group shares the idea of choosing without a rule.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ran-/rand- 的读音，其中两个词还真有词源关系；第二组共享“不按规则地选择”这一观念。

entries.definition: money paid to free a captive. It is unrelated in meaning but shares the odd -m spelling change with random.
entries.definitionCN: 赎金。意义无关，但与 random 共享那个奇特的 -n 变 -m 拼写变化。

entries.definition: the Middle English noun for 'rush, impetuosity' from which at random was shortened.
entries.definitionCN: 中古英语名词，意为“冲势、猛劲”，at random 即由它缩来。

entries.definition: a unit of currency, or a random value in computing. It looks like a clipped random but is a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: 货币单位，或计算中的随机值。它看起来像 random 的缩写，其实是另一个词。

entries.definition: in a random manner. The adverb looks like the adjective with a tail.
entries.definitionCN: 随机地。这个副词看起来就像形容词多了一条尾巴。

entries.definition: decided by personal choice or impulse rather than reason. It stresses the chooser's freedom, while random stresses the absence of pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 任意的；专断的。它强调选择者的自由，而 random 强调图案的缺失。

entries.definition: with no plan or order, happening as it may. It is close to random but more judgemental.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然的；杂乱的。它接近 random，但更带贬义。

entries.definition: an event that happens without design. It names the cause, while random names the lack of pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然；机会。它命名原因，而 random 命名缺乏规律。

entries.definition: done without care or intention. It suits a casual remark, not a random sample.
entries.definitionCN: 随便的；漫不经心的。它适合一句随口的话，不适合随机样本。

entries.definition: done without choosing carefully, affecting everyone or everything alike.
entries.definitionCN: 不加区别的；滥施的。

normalIntro.en: The real links are speed and horses: Old French randon 'rush', the phrase at random, and ransom's matching -m spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的联想是速度与马：古法语 randon“冲势”、短语 at random，以及 ransom 那同样的 -m 拼写。

normal.en: random and randon: the old noun meant 'rush, impetuosity', so at random first meant 'at full speed'.
normal.cn: random 与 randon：这个古名词意为“冲势、猛劲”，所以 at random 最初意为“全速地”。

normal.en: Think of a horse with no rider: it runs fast and goes nowhere in particular.
normal.cn: 想象一匹没有骑手的马：跑得飞快，却哪里也不去。

normal.en: random access memory does not read in order; it jumps, like a shopper who knows every aisle.
normal.cn: 随机存取存储器不按顺序读；它直接跳，像一个熟悉每条货架的购物者。

normal.en: Random and ransom share the -m: both changed from -n, and neither tells you why.
normal.cn: random 与 ransom 共享那个 -m：两者都由 -n 变来，谁也说不出原因。

normal.en: A random sample is chance made fair: everyone gets the same lottery ticket.
normal.cn: 随机样本是把偶然变得公平：每个人都拿到同样的彩票。

abstract.en: The core is released control: no hand on the reins, no target in sight.
abstract.cn: 核心是放开的控制：缰绳上没有手，视野里没有靶。

abstract.en: Speed, chance, pattern, order: random denies a different thing in each field.
abstract.cn: 速度、偶然、图案、次序：random 在每个领域否认的东西都不一样。

abstract.en: A statistical word built from a galloping horse is the best proof that metaphor becomes method.
abstract.cn: 一个由奔马构成的统计词，正是“隐喻变成方法”的最好证据。

examples.en: The names were chosen at random from a hat.
examples.cn: 名字是从帽子里随机抽出来的。

examples.en: A random error in the data can ruin the whole model.
examples.cn: 数据中的一个随机误差就能毁掉整个模型。

examples.en: She met a random stranger who turned out to be her new boss.
examples.cn: 她偶然遇到一个陌生人，结果竟是她的新上司。

dict_mnemonic.text: ran（跑）+ dom（= dumb 哑的）—— 一匹又跑又哑的马，没有方向地乱冲 → random 随机的；胡乱的

root: 源自古法语 randon“冲势、猛劲”、randir“快跑”，上溯法兰克语 *rant 与原始日耳曼语 *randa“奔跑”，与 run 同族；核心是“一匹全速奔跑却不辨方向的马”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one horse: it gallops without a target, so nothing is aimed, nothing repeats, nothing is in order — and in computing the same word means 'without a fixed sequence'.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一匹马：它没有目标地狂奔，于是没有瞄准、没有重复、没有次序；在计算机里，同一个词就表示“没有固定顺序”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horse galloping with no rider and no destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：一匹没有骑手、也没有目的地的奔马。

branches.en: THE GALLOP: the old phrase 'at speed' and the chance encounter it became.
branches.cn: 奔驰：古老的“全速”短语，以及由此变成的偶然相遇。

branches.en: NO TARGET, NO PATTERN: unaimed action and irregular shape.
branches.cn: 无靶、无纹：没有瞄准的动作，与没有规律的形状。

branches.en: NO FIXED ORDER: memory that jumps, and numbers made by an imitation of chance.
branches.cn: 无固定次序：会跳的存储器，以及模仿偶然造出的数字。

branches.en: FAIR CHANCE: the sample in which every case has the same ticket.
branches.cn: 公平的偶然：每个个体都拿到同样一张票的样本。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDER: the stranger with no link, and the slang name for someone who does not belong.
branches.cn: 局外人：毫无联系的陌生人，以及指称“不属于这里的人”的俚语。

intro.en: Random has no living prefix or suffix in English; it is a whole French noun that became an adjective. Its family shows -ly, -ness, -ize, -ization and the compound random-access.
intro.cn: random 在英语里没有活的前缀或后缀；它是一个整体借来的法语名词，后来变成形容词。它的词族展示 -ly、-ness、-ize、-ization 以及复合词 random-access。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor: the line runs from Frankish *rant through Old French randon and randir to English. Latin is absent from this word's family tree.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁祖先：这条线从法兰克语 *rant 经古法语 randon、randir 到英语。这个词的家谱里没有拉丁语。

items.structure: Old French randon (rush) + English adjective use
items.example: The survey used a random sample of readers.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查使用了随机读者样本。

items.example: The files were randomly assigned to each group.
items.exampleCN: 文件被随机分配给每一组。

items.meaning: the quality of having no pattern
items.example: True randomness is hard to produce by machine.
items.exampleCN: 真正的随机性很难由机器产生。

items.meaning: to arrange in a random order
items.example: The software randomizes the order of the questions.
items.exampleCN: 这个软件会随机打乱题目的顺序。

items.meaning: the act of making something random
items.example: Randomization reduces bias in clinical trials.
items.exampleCN: 随机化可减少临床试验中的偏倚。

items.meaning: a device or program that produces random choices
items.example: The teacher used an online randomizer to call on students.
items.exampleCN: 老师用在线随机器点名。

items.meaning: direct reading of any memory location
items.example: Solid-state drives offer fast random access.
items.exampleCN: 固态硬盘提供快速的随机存取。

items.meaning: a number with no predictable order
items.example: The password generator starts with a random number.
items.exampleCN: 密码生成器以一个随机数开始。

items.example: She opened the book at random and began to read.
items.exampleCN: 她随手翻开书，开始读起来。

definition_zh: 下渗；入渗；（军事或秘密的）渗透；浸润
definition_en: the movement of water into soil or rock through the surface; also the secret entry of people or ideas into an organisation
core_image: 雨水停在松土表面，先是一层暗色湿斑，随后整片土色变深，水沿着颗粒缝隙向下走
scene: 雨停之后，坡上的水不再往低处流，而是一点点钻进松土，表层很快变暗。 After the rain, infiltration carries the water into the loose soil instead of down the slope.
sceneCN: 这里 infiltration 指「地表水进入土壤或岩层的下渗过程」（第 1 个义项：水从地表穿过界面进入多孔介质）；句意为雨停后水不再沿坡流走，而是渗进松土。可辨识物件：坡面、湿斑、松土颗粒、下渗箭头。

senses.title: Water entering the soil
senses.titleCN: 下渗：水从地表进入土壤
senses.definition: the process by which water on the ground surface passes into soil or rock
senses.definitionCN: 地表水穿过界面进入土壤或岩石的过程
senses.example: Sandy soil allows rapid infiltration after a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 沙质土壤在暴雨后下渗很快。
senses.why: The word begins with in-, movement inward, and that is exactly what happens at the surface: water stops being runoff and becomes soil water.
senses.whyCN: 这个词以表示「向内」的 in- 开头，而地表发生的正是这件事：水不再是径流，而变成土壤水。

senses.title: Rate and capacity
senses.definition: the speed at which water enters the soil, and the maximum the soil can absorb
senses.definitionCN: 水进入土壤的速度，以及土壤能吸收的最大量
senses.example: Heavy rain exceeded the infiltration capacity, so water ran off.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨超过了下渗容量，因此水从地表流走。
senses.why: Once entry has a speed, it has a ceiling: the soil can only open so fast, and everything above that ceiling becomes surface flow.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「进入」有了速度，也就有了上限：土壤开口只能那么快，超过上限的部分就变成地表流。

senses.title: Entry versus percolation
senses.definition: the entry step at the surface, distinguished from the downward travel of water inside the soil
senses.definitionCN: 发生在表面的进入环节，区别于水在土壤内部的向下运移
senses.example: Infiltration is the door; percolation is the corridor behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 入渗是门，渗滤是门后的走廊。
senses.why: Hydrology separates the two because a surface can be sealed at the door while the soil behind it is still able to transmit water.
senses.whyCN: 水文学把两者分开，因为地表这道「门」可以被封住，而门后的土壤仍然能够导水。

senses.title: Military penetration
senses.definition: the movement of soldiers or units through or past an enemy line in small groups
senses.definitionCN: 小股部队穿过或绕过敌方防线的行动
senses.example: The patrol reported infiltration across the border at night.
senses.exampleCN: 巡逻队报告夜间有人越过边界渗透。
senses.why: The military sense keeps the physical image: small units pass through a line the way water passes through pores, without breaking it.
senses.whyCN: 军事义保留了物理意象：小股部队像水穿过孔隙一样穿过多道防线，而不把防线打破。

senses.title: Secret entry into an organisation
senses.titleCN: 秘密潜入：进入组织内部
senses.definition: the placement of agents or members inside a group in order to influence or report on it
senses.definitionCN: 把人员安插进某个团体，以便影响它或向其汇报
senses.example: The infiltration of the union took years to uncover.
senses.exampleCN: 对工会的渗透用了多年才被揭出。
senses.why: Here the pores are people: entry is gradual, quiet and distributed, which is why it is harder to detect than an outright attack.
senses.whyCN: 这里孔隙换成了人：进入是渐进的、安静的、分散的，所以比正面攻击更难发现。

senses.title: Medical infiltration
senses.titleCN: 医学浸润：药液或细胞渗进组织
senses.definition: the spread of a liquid or of cells into surrounding tissue
senses.definitionCN: 液体或细胞扩散进入周围组织
senses.example: The dentist used local infiltration to numb the gum.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医用局部浸润麻醉牙龈。
senses.why: The same inward movement appears in the body: an anaesthetic or a tumour spreads into tissue rather than staying in one place.
senses.whyCN: 同样的向内运动也出现在身体里：麻醉剂或肿瘤扩散进入组织，而不是停留在一处。

senses.title: Ideas entering a system
senses.titleCN: 观念渗透：慢慢进入一个体系
senses.definition: the gradual spread of ideas, terms or practices into an institution or culture
senses.definitionCN: 观念、术语或做法逐渐进入某个机构或文化
senses.example: The infiltration of market language into schools worried the teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 市场语言渗入学校让教师们感到担忧。
senses.why: Ideas travel like water: they do not announce themselves, they enter through many small openings and change the colour of everything.
senses.whyCN: 观念的传播像水：它们不宣告自己，而是从许多小口进入，最后改变整体的颜色。

senses.title: Impregnation of a material
senses.titleCN: 材料浸渗：把另一种物质灌进孔隙
senses.definition: the filling of pores in a solid with resin, oil or another substance
senses.definitionCN: 用树脂、油或其他物质填充固体中的孔隙
senses.example: Vacuum infiltration sealed the porous casting.
senses.exampleCN: 真空浸渗把多孔铸件封住了。
senses.why: In engineering the direction is deliberate: something is made to enter the pores on purpose, so the porous body becomes solid.
senses.whyCN: 在工程中方向是被刻意安排的：让人为地把某种物质送入孔隙，使多孔体变得致密。

intro.en: Infiltration is a Medieval Latin noun built on filtrum, a word for felt that Latin borrowed from Germanic. The English noun appears in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: infiltration 是建立在中古拉丁语 filtrum 之上的名词，而 filtrum 是拉丁语从日耳曼语借来的「毛毡」一词。英语名词在十七世纪出现。年代为约数。

items.en: Filtrum meant felt or a felt strainer; it is generally considered a borrowing into Latin from a Germanic word related to German Filz, felt.
items.cn: filtrum 指毛毡或毛毡滤器；一般认为它是拉丁语从日耳曼语借入的词，与德语 Filz「毛毡」相关。

items.en: The prefix in- marks movement into or onto something, as in influx and inject, and it directs the whole action inward.
items.cn: 前缀 in- 表示进入或向某物之上，如 influx 与 inject，它把整个动作指向内部。

items.en: Medieval Latin infiltrare meant to filter in or to pass through a strainer, a technical verb of alchemy and medicine before it became a noun.
items.cn: 中古拉丁语 infiltrare 意为「滤入」或「穿过滤器」，在成为名词之前是炼金术与医学的技术动词。

items.en: English infiltration first names the action of filtering in, then extends to military penetration and later to soil water entering the ground.
items.cn: 英语 infiltration 先指「滤入」的动作，随后扩展到军事渗透，再后来用于水进入土壤。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of each sense): the earliest English use is not fixed precisely, and the order in which the military and hydrological senses developed is only approximately dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（各义项首见年代）：最早的英语用例未被精确确定，军事义与水文义的发展先后也只有大致年代。

note.en: The first group holds words that differ by a letter or a suffix; the second holds the water processes most often confused with infiltration.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个字母或后缀的词；第二组是常与下渗混淆的水文过程。

entries.definition: Filtering alone, with no inward prefix: the process of passing a liquid through a filter.
entries.definitionCN: 只有「过滤」，没有表示向内的前缀：让液体通过滤器。

entries.definition: A change in the form of a word or in pitch; it has nothing to do with filtering.
entries.definitionCN: 词形或语调的变化；与过滤毫无关系。

entries.definition: To enter by passing through pores or lines; the noun for the action is infiltration.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过孔隙或防线进入；其动作名词为 infiltration。

entries.definition: The downward movement of water within soil after it has already entered.
entries.definitionCN: 水进入土壤之后在土体内部的向下运动。

entries.definition: Water that fails to enter and flows over the surface instead.
entries.definitionCN: 没能进入土壤、改沿地表流走的水。

entries.definition: Slow movement of water through soil, rock or a structure, often unintended.
entries.definitionCN: 水缓慢穿过土壤、岩石或结构物，常为意外的渗漏。

entries.definition: Entry into or through something by force or depth; it lacks the porous, gradual image.
entries.definitionCN: 以力量或深度进入或穿过某物；没有多孔、渐进的高象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the felt strainer behind the word, the in- prefix, and the pair with percolation.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：词后的「毛毡滤器」、in- 前缀，以及与渗滤的成对关系。

normal.en: The root filtrum is felt: the first filters were mats of felt that let water through.
normal.cn: 词根 filtrum 是毛毡：最早的滤器就是让水穿过的毛毡垫。

normal.en: in- points inward, so infiltration is entry, not exit.
normal.cn: in- 指向内部，所以下渗是「进入」，不是「出去」。

normal.en: Infiltration is the door, percolation is the corridor, runoff is the water that never got in.
normal.cn: 下渗是门，渗滤是走廊，径流是从没进门的那些水。

normal.en: In the army the line is the surface and small units are the water.
normal.cn: 在军队里，防线就是地表，小股部队就是水。

normal.en: The medical sense is the same word: an anaesthetic filters into the tissue around the needle.
normal.cn: 医学义是同一个词：麻醉剂从针尖渗入周围组织。

abstract.en: Abstractly, infiltration is entry without breaking: the boundary stays intact while something passes through it.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，渗透是不破坏边界的进入：某物穿过去，而边界仍然完整。

abstract.en: It is also a slow takeover: many small entries, each harmless, add up to a changed whole.
abstract.cn: 它也是一种缓慢的接管：许多单独无害的小进入，累积起来就改变了整体。

abstract.en: Anything that enters quietly through many openings — water, ideas, people — follows this pattern.
abstract.cn: 任何从许多开口安静进入的东西——水、观念、人——都遵循这个模式。

examples.en: Compacted soil loses infiltration capacity and sends the rain straight to the river.
examples.cn: 压实的土壤失去下渗能力，把雨水直接送进河里。

examples.en: The report warned of infiltration by foreign agents in the ministry.
examples.cn: 报告警告该部门存在外国人员的渗透。

examples.en: Resin infiltration turned the porous metal part into a pressure-tight component.
examples.cn: 树脂浸渗把多孔金属件变成了耐压部件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印（in，往里）+ 滤（filtr）+ 渗」——水往滤垫里进去 → 下渗、渗透

root: 中古拉丁语 in-「向内」+ filtrum「毛毡、滤垫」（拉丁语借自日耳曼语）+ -atio（动作名词后缀）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe entry through a boundary: water into soil, its rate, its contrast with percolation, soldiers through a line, agents into a group, fluid into tissue, ideas into a system, and resin into pores.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「穿过边界进入」：水进入土壤、其速率、与渗滤的对照、士兵穿过防线、人员进入组织、液体进入组织、观念进入体系、树脂进入孔隙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark wet patch spreading downward into loose soil, the surface itself unbroken.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块暗色湿斑向松土内部扩散，而地表本身并未破裂。

branches.en: THE DOOR AND ITS SPEED: entry happens at a rate, and the rate has a ceiling.
branches.cn: 门与速度：进入有速率，而速率有上限。

branches.en: DOOR VERSUS CORRIDOR: infiltration is crossing the surface, percolation is travelling inside.
branches.cn: 门与走廊：下渗是穿过表面，渗滤是在内部行进。

branches.en: LINES AND ORGANISATIONS: small units pass through defences; agents pass into groups.
branches.cn: 防线与组织：小股部队穿过多道防线；人员进入团体。

branches.en: TISSUE AND CULTURE: fluid and ideas both spread quietly into a body.
branches.cn: 组织与文化：液体与观念都安静地扩散进一个整体。

branches.en: DELIBERATE FILLING: engineering reverses the worry and makes entry useful.
branches.cn: 有意的填充：工程把这种担忧反转，让进入变得有用。

intro.en: Infiltration has a prefix, a root and a noun suffix, and the root also builds the everyday word filter.
intro.cn: infiltration 由前缀、词根与名词后缀构成，而这个词根也构成日常词 filter。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is filtrum, felt, which Latin took from Germanic. Its Latin verbs were infiltrare and its nouns infiltratio; English filter descends from the same Medieval Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 filtrum「毛毡」，这个词是拉丁语从日耳曼语借入的。其拉丁动词为 infiltrare，名词为 infiltratio；英语 filter 也出自同一中古拉丁词。

items.structure: filter (Medieval Latin filtrum, felt, from Germanic)
items.meaning: a material or device that lets liquid through while holding back solids
items.meaningCN: 让液体通过而拦住固体的材料或装置
items.example: The filter removed the sediment.
items.exampleCN: 滤器除去了沉积物。

items.meaning: passing a liquid through a filter
items.meaningCN: 让液体通过滤器的过程
items.example: Filtration cleaned the sample.
items.exampleCN: 过滤净化了样品。

items.meaning: the liquid that has passed through a filter
items.meaningCN: 已经穿过过滤器的液体
items.example: The filtrate was clear.
items.exampleCN: 滤液是清澈的。

items.meaning: to enter through pores or lines
items.example: Water infiltrates the sandy bank.
items.exampleCN: 水渗入沙质河岸。

items.meaning: the act or result of entering through a boundary
items.meaningCN: 穿过边界进入的动作或结果
items.example: Infiltration rose after the grass was removed.
items.exampleCN: 草被清除后下渗量上升。

items.example: The infiltrator posed as a volunteer.
items.exampleCN: 那名渗透者冒充志愿者。

items.meaning: tending to spread into surrounding tissue
items.meaningCN: 倾向于向周围组织扩散的
items.example: The growth was infiltrative rather than contained.
items.exampleCN: 这个增生是浸润性的，而不是局限的。

items.meaning: downward travel of water inside soil
items.meaningCN: 水在土体内部的向下运移
items.example: Percolation continues long after infiltration stops.
items.exampleCN: 下渗停止之后，渗滤仍持续很久。

items.example: Seepage weakened the dam's base.
items.exampleCN: 渗漏削弱了坝基。

latinEntries.structure: filtrum (Medieval Latin, felt or strainer, from Germanic)

latinEntries.meaning: to filter in, to pass through a strainer

definition_zh: 族群；由共同祖先、语言或文化认同构成的人群；国家内部被承认的族裔群体
definition_en: a community of people who share ancestry, language or culture and are recognised as a distinct group
core_image: 一张村落分布图上，几个不同颜色的区块沿河谷排开，每个区块有自己的语言与节日
scene: 这个山谷里最大的一群人说着一种别处听不到的语言，节日也与他处不同。 The valley's largest ethnic group speaks a language found nowhere else.
sceneCN: 这里 ethnic group 指由共同祖先、语言或文化构成的人群（第 1 个义项：作为共同体）；句意为这个山谷里最大的族群说着一种别处没有的语言。

collocations.phrase: an ethnic group within the state

derivatives.zh: 族群的（由希腊 ethnos 经拉丁进入，限定 group 的属性）
族群身份（由基础形容词加表抽象属性的名词后缀而来，由属性转指抽象身份）
群；组（经法语来自意大利语，指聚在一起的一簇人或物）
分组；归类（由基础动词加表活动或结果的名词后缀而来，由动作转指结果）
重新集结（由基础动词加表再次的前缀而来，由「聚成一组」转指「再次聚拢」）

senses.title: A community of shared origin
senses.definition: a people who trace common ancestry and share language, custom or memory
senses.definitionCN: 追溯共同祖先、共享语言、习俗或记忆的一群人
senses.example: Each ethnic group in the valley keeps its own harvest song.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里的每个族群都保留自己的收割歌。
senses.why: The phrase joins a people to a body: group supplies the boundary, ethnic supplies what the boundary is drawn around.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组把人群与团体结合起来：团体提供边界，族群属性提供边界所圈定的内容。

senses.title: A recognised minority
senses.definition: a group officially or socially recognised as distinct within a larger state
senses.definitionCN: 在一个较大国家内被官方或社会承认为有区别的群体
senses.example: The constitution names five ethnic groups with protected rights.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法列出五个受权利保护的族群。
senses.why: Recognition is a legal act: a people becomes an ethnic group in law when the state names it.
senses.whyCN: 承认是一种法律行为：当国家点名时，一群人才在法律上成为族群。

senses.title: The analytic unit
senses.definition: the unit anthropologists and sociologists use to compare kinship, language and ritual
senses.definitionCN: 人类学者与社会学者用来比较亲属、语言与仪式的单位
senses.example: The study compared three ethnic groups across one generation.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究在一代人之内比较了三个族群。
senses.why: Research needs countable units; the phrase turns a fluid people into something that can be placed side by side.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要可数的单位；这个词组把流动的人群变成可以并排比较的对象。

senses.title: Self-identified membership
senses.definition: a group constituted by people who say they belong to it
senses.definitionCN: 由自称属于其中的人所构成的群体
senses.example: The ethnic group was defined by self-identification, not by a list.
senses.exampleCN: 这个族群靠自我认同来界定，而不是靠一份名单。
senses.why: Modern practice prefers the insider's claim; the group exists where members say it does.
senses.whyCN: 现代实践更看重内部人的主张；成员说它在，它就在。

senses.title: The majority group
senses.definition: the dominant ethnic group whose language and customs set the national norm
senses.definitionCN: 其语言与习俗设定国家规范的占主导地位的族群
senses.example: The majority ethnic group rarely notices its own ethnicity.
senses.exampleCN: 多数族群很少注意到自己的族群性。
senses.why: The phrase is not reserved for minorities: a majority is also an ethnic group, only one whose marks are invisible to itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组并非只用于少数群体：多数也是一个族群，只是它的标记对自己不可见。

senses.title: A political actor
senses.definition: a group organised to make claims on the state in the name of its people
senses.definitionCN: 以本族群之名向国家提出主张的组织化群体
senses.example: The ethnic group formed a party after the census.
senses.exampleCN: 普查之后，这个族群组成了一个政党。
senses.why: When a group acquires representatives, a cultural category becomes a bargaining unit.
senses.whyCN: 当一个群体有了代表，文化类别就变成了谈判单位。

senses.title: A census category
senses.definition: a box on official forms that counts people by ethnic membership
senses.definitionCN: 官方表格上按族群归属清点人口的选项
senses.example: The census lists the ethnic group under a new label.
senses.exampleCN: 普查用一种新标签列出这个族群。
senses.why: Counting requires a name and a fixed list, so the state's version of the group may differ from the group's own.
senses.whyCN: 清点需要一个名称和固定清单，因此国家版本的族群可能与族群自身的版本不同。

senses.title: Across borders
senses.definition: a people whose members live in several states and keep ties across borders
senses.definitionCN: 成员分布在若干国家、并维持跨境联系的群体
senses.example: The ethnic group operates schools in four countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个族群在四个国家办学校。
senses.why: Migration splits a group geographically without splitting its identity, so the phrase can cross state lines.
senses.whyCN: 迁徙把群体在地理上分开，却没有分开其认同，因此这个词组可以跨越国界。

intro.en: Ethnic group joins Greek ethnos 'people' (through ethnikos and Latin ethnicus) to group, a word borrowed from French and probably from Italian. The compound is a modern social-science term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ethnic group 把希腊 ethnos「人群」（经 ethnikos 与拉丁 ethnicus）与 group 组合起来；后者借自法语，可能源自意大利语。这个复合词是现代社会科学术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Italian gruppo meant 'a cluster, a knot of things'. It is often derived from grappo 'knot', but the origin is uncertain and a Germanic source has also been proposed.
items.cn: 意大利语 gruppo 意为「一簇、一团」。它常被追溯到 grappo「结」，但来源不确定，也有人提出日耳曼语来源。

items.en: French groupe entered the language in the seventeenth century from Italian and named a cluster of figures in painting before it named people.
items.cn: 法语 groupe 在十七世纪从意大利语进入，先指绘画中聚在一起的人物群像，后指人群。

items.en: English group followed in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, widening from art to any set of things or persons gathered together.
items.cn: 英语 group 在十七、十八世纪跟进，从艺术用语扩展到任何聚在一起的事物或人。

items.en: Ethnos 'people, nation' supplied the first element; ethnikos and Latin ethnicus carried it into European languages.
items.cn: ethnos「人群、民族」提供前一成分；ethnikos 与拉丁 ethnicus 把它带入欧洲各语言。

items.en: In the twentieth century ethnic group became the standard unit for comparing peoples without the older language of race.
items.cn: 二十世纪，ethnic group 成为比较各人群的标准单位，取代了较早的种族语言。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of gruppo is unresolved, and the pre-Greek origin of ethnos remains unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：gruppo 的来源未有定论；ethnos 在希腊语之前的来源仍然不明。

note.en: Group one separates the parts of the phrase; group two holds other units for describing peoples.
note.cn: 第一组区分词组的组成部分；第二组是描述人群的其他单位。

entries.definition: The abstract belonging; the group is the people who hold it.
entries.definitionCN: 抽象的归属属性；族群则是持有这一属性的人们。

entries.definition: Describing a people; it needs a noun such as group to name the people itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述人群的；需要像 group 这样的名词才能命名人群本身。

entries.definition: Any set of persons or things; without ethnic it could be a chess club.
entries.definitionCN: 任何一组人或物；没有 ethnic 时也可能指棋社。

entries.definition: The arrangement of things into groups; it names a classification, not a people.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物分组的安排；它命名分类行为，而非一群人。

entries.definition: A group sharing a place or interest; it need not have common ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 共享地点或利益的一群人；不一定有共同祖先。

entries.definition: A people claiming statehood or a whole state; larger and more political than an ethnic group.
entries.definitionCN: 主张国家地位的人群，或整个国家；比族群更大、更具政治性。

entries.definition: Any group smaller than the majority; ethnicity is one basis for minority status, not the only one.
entries.definitionCN: 任何小于多数群体的群体；族群性是少数地位的依据之一，而非唯一依据。

entries.definition: A kinship unit within a larger people; narrower than an ethnic group and based on descent lines.
entries.definitionCN: 较大人群内部的亲属单位；比族群窄，且以世系为基础。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots, real compounds and real social-science phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根、真实的复合词与真实的社会科学说法。

normal.en: Ethnic names the people, group names the boundary around them.
normal.cn: ethnic 命名人群，group 命名圈住他们的边界。

normal.en: Group first meant a cluster in a painting, then any cluster of people.
normal.cn: group 先指绘画中的一群人物，再指任何聚在一起的人。

normal.en: A majority is also an ethnic group; it simply does not notice its own marks.
normal.cn: 多数群体也是一个族群，只是它不注意自己的标记。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the analysis: ethnic group boundaries, relations between ethnic groups, the largest ethnic group.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出分析：族群边界、族群之间的关系、最大的族群。

normal.en: The plural ethnic groups is standard for comparisons and census lists.
normal.cn: 比较与普查清单中，复数 ethnic groups 是标准用法。

abstract.en: Picture a map coloured in blocks, where each colour also has a song.
abstract.cn: 想象一张用色块涂成的地图，每种颜色还各有一首歌。

abstract.en: Picture a circle drawn around a people, and the people moving across the line.
abstract.cn: 想象在人群周围画一个圈，而人不断越过那条线。

abstract.en: Picture a form with a box that fits one family badly and another family too well.
abstract.cn: 想象表格上的一个框，对一户人家太窄，对另一户又太宽。

examples.en: The ethnic group has kept its own calendar for centuries.
examples.cn: 这个族群数百年来保留着自己的历法。

examples.en: Census categories often split one ethnic group into two.
examples.cn: 普查类别常把一个族群拆成两个。

examples.en: Schools teach the history of every ethnic group in the province.
examples.cn: 学校教授本省每一个族群的历史。

dict_mnemonic.text: ethnic（族群的）+ group（聚成一群）＝ 因共同来源而聚成的一群人；记「一种语言，一圈边界，一张表格」。

root: ethnic 源自希腊 ethnos「人群」，更早来源不确定，经 ethnikos 与拉丁 ethnicus 传入英语；group 经法语来自意大利语 gruppo「一簇」，其来源不确定，或与「结」有关，或另有日耳曼语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a shared-origin community to legal minority, analytic unit, self-identification, majority, political actor, census box and cross-border people.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从共享来源的共同体，移到法律上的少数、分析单位、自我认同、多数群体、政治行动者、普查选项与跨境人群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coloured block on a map that also has a language, a festival and a line around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一个色块，同时拥有一种语言、一个节日和一条围绕它的线。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY: ancestry, language and memory held in common.
branches.cn: 共同体：共同持有的祖先、语言与记忆。

branches.en: THE LEGAL NAME: the state recognises the group and thereby fixes it.
branches.cn: 法律名称：国家承认这个群体，并因此把它固定下来。

branches.en: UNIT AND SELF-CLAIM: research counts it, while members say they belong.
branches.cn: 单位与自我主张：研究把它计数，成员则说自己属于其中。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE MAJORITY: dominance hides its own ethnicity.
branches.cn: 看不见的多数：主导地位掩盖了自身的族群性。

branches.en: CLAIM, BOX AND BORDER: a party, a census category, and a people spread over several states.
branches.cn: 主张、表格与国界：一个政党、一个普查类别，以及分布于数个国家的人群。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived adjective to a French-derived noun; both halves are common words in modern English.
intro.cn: 这个词组把希腊来源的形容词与法语来源的名词结合起来，两半都是现代英语常用词。

latinIntro.en: Only the first element is Greek-Latin: ethnos through ethnikos and ethnicus. Group is French and Italian, with an uncertain deeper origin.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前一成分属希腊—拉丁来源：ethnos 经 ethnikos 与 ethnicus。group 属法语与意大利语来源，更深来源不确定。

items.example: Ethnic lines are drawn by history.
items.exampleCN: 族群界线由历史画出。

items.example: The form asks about ethnicity.
items.exampleCN: 表格询问族群身份。

items.meaning: a cluster of people or things
items.example: The group meets on Sundays.
items.exampleCN: 这个群体周日见面。

items.example: The grouping follows language, not border.
items.exampleCN: 这种分组依据语言，而非国界。

items.example: The pupils sat in grouped desks.
items.exampleCN: 学生们坐在分组排列的课桌旁。

items.example: The marchers regrouped at the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 游行者在桥边重新集结。

items.meaning: the behaviour of people in a group
items.example: Group dynamics changed when the room filled.
items.exampleCN: 房间坐满后，群体动力发生了变化。

items.meaning: a smaller group inside a larger one
items.meaningCN: 子群；较大群体内的小群体
items.example: Each subgroup kept a separate dialect.
items.exampleCN: 每个子群保留了一种不同的方言。

definition_zh: 丰富的；充裕的；慷慨的
definition_en: large in amount; generous in giving
core_image: 秋日谷仓前堆成小山的麦袋与果篮，主人抓起果子大把大把往客人怀里塞
scene: 丰收季农庄开门迎客。 The farmer gave every visitor a bountiful basket of apples and honey.
sceneCN: 这里 bountiful 是「丰富的、慷慨的」（第 2 个义项：慷慨给予）；句意是农夫给每位访客都送上满满一篮苹果和蜂蜜。

derivatives.zh: 由同根名词构成，义为「慷慨赠予；赏金」
同根形容词变体，义为「丰饶的；慷慨的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「丰盛地；慷慨地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「丰盛；慷慨」

senses.title: Existing in large quantity
senses.definition: present in great amounts, more than enough
senses.definitionCN: 数量极大，绰绰有余
senses.example: The valley enjoys a bountiful rainfall every year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷每年降水丰沛。
senses.why: The root bounty once meant goodness, and goodness in supply shows up first as sheer abundance.
senses.whyCN: 词根 bounty 本义为「善」，供应上的「善」首先表现为单纯的数量充裕。

senses.title: Giving freely and generously
senses.definition: willing to give more than is expected or required
senses.definitionCN: 乐于付出超出预期或所需的给予
senses.example: The charity was bountiful to the flooded village.
senses.exampleCN: 慈善组织对被淹的村庄慷慨解囊。
senses.why: Abundance in supply turns naturally into abundance in giving, since only the rich in goods can give richly.
senses.whyCN: 供应的充裕自然转化为给予的慷慨，因为只有财物富足者才能慷慨相赠。

senses.title: Producing abundantly
senses.definition: yielding large crops or plentiful output
senses.definitionCN: 产出大量作物或丰富的成果
senses.example: The bountiful orchard fed three villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这片丰产的果园养活了三个村庄。
senses.why: What is abundant in a producer is its yield, so the adjective attaches to fields, orchards, and lands.
senses.whyCN: 对生产者而言，「充裕」体现为产量，于是该形容词常用于田地、果园、土地。

senses.title: Rich in variety as well as amount
senses.definition: abundant across many kinds, not just one
senses.definitionCN: 不仅量大，而且种类多样
senses.example: The bountiful menu offered forty dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 丰盛的菜单上有四十道菜。
senses.why: Plenty of one thing invites plenty of many things, extending the image from bulk to spread.
senses.whyCN: 一物之丰引来众物之丰，意象由「成堆」扩展为「满席」。

senses.title: Overflowing emotionally
senses.definition: full to overflowing, as of feelings expressed freely
senses.definitionCN: 情感充沛、尽兴流露的
senses.example: Her bountiful laughter filled the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她爽朗的笑声充满了大厅。
senses.why: The picture of a vessel running over transfers from goods to emotions.
senses.whyCN: 容器满溢的画面由财物转移到情感上。

senses.title: Freely bestowed, as of rewards
senses.definition: granted in generous amounts, as rewards or payments
senses.definitionCN: 以大方数额发放的，如奖励或报酬
senses.example: The informer received a bountiful reward.
senses.exampleCN: 告密者获得了一笔丰厚的赏金。
senses.why: The old noun bounty survives in prize money, and the adjective keeps this concrete use.
senses.whyCN: 古名词 bounty 仍存于赏金义，形容词保留了这一具体用法。

senses.title: Splendid in appearance
senses.definition: rich and impressive to the eye, as of displays or feasts
senses.definitionCN: 看上去富丽可观，如陈列或盛宴
senses.example: The bountiful table gleamed with silver and fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 丰盛的餐桌在银器和水果的映照下熠熠生辉。
senses.why: Abundance made visible becomes splendor, the sense completing from quantity to impression.
senses.whyCN: 充裕一旦可见即成华彩，词义由数量完成到观感的过渡。

senses.title: Readily available in nature
senses.definition: supplied freely by nature without human effort
senses.definitionCN: 无需人力而由自然大量供应的
senses.example: The coast is bountiful with fish and kelp.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海岸盛产鱼类和海藻。
senses.why: Nature gives without being asked, the oldest picture behind the word's sense of unearned plenty.
senses.whyCN: 自然无偿给予，这正是该词「不劳而获的丰饶」这层古义背后的最初画面。

intro.en: Bountiful descends, through Old French, from Latin bonus, good, by way of the noun bounty.
intro.cn: bountiful 经由古法语，溯源自拉丁语 bonus（好），其名词中介为 bounty。

items.en: The reconstructed root deu- meant to show favor or worship, the deep source of Latin bonus.
items.cn: 重构词根 deu- 意为「施恩、敬奉」，是拉丁语 bonus 的深层来源。

items.en: Latin bonus meant good, and bonitas meant goodness, both common in classical writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bonus 意为「好的」，bonitas 意为「善」，均见于古典文献。

items.en: Old French bonte meant goodness and later liberality, borrowed from Latin bonitas.
items.cn: 古法语 bonte 意为「善」，后转指「慷慨」，借自拉丁语 bonitas。

items.en: Middle English took bounty from Old French, first meaning goodness, then generous giving and reward.
items.cn: 中古英语自古法语借入 bounty，先表「善」，后表「慷慨赠予与赏金」。

items.en: The adjective bountiful formed in the fifteenth century from bounty plus -ful.
items.cn: 十五世纪由 bounty 加后缀 -ful 构成形容词 bountiful。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the abundance sense and the generosity sense, with bounteous as a literary twin.
items.cn: 现代英语兼存「丰饶」与「慷慨」二义，另有书面色彩的同义词 bounteous。

note.en: Bountiful sits between plenty and generosity; watch the spelling beside bounty and boundary.
note.cn: bountiful 介于「充足」与「慷慨」之间；注意与 bounty、boundary 的拼写区分。

entries.definition: generosity or a reward paid by authorities
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨；赏金；同根名词

entries.definition: a literary equivalent of bountiful
entries.definitionCN: 丰饶的；慷慨的；同根书面变体

entries.definition: a line marking a limit
entries.definitionCN: 边界；与 bountiful 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: pleasing to the eye
entries.definitionCN: 美丽的；仅 -tiful 部分拼写相仿，词源无关

entries.definition: existing in large amounts
entries.definitionCN: 丰富的；拼写结构相仿但词源不同

entries.definition: existing in very large quantities
entries.definitionCN: 大量的；侧重数量，bountiful 兼含慷慨之意

entries.definition: willing to give freely
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨的；侧重给予态度

entries.definition: giving or spending generously, sometimes too much
entries.definitionCN: 奢华大方的；程度比 bountiful 更强

entries.definition: given or produced in great amounts
entries.definitionCN: 大量的；常指喷涌而出之物

entries.definition: large in number or volume
entries.definitionCN: 丰富的；多用于文字或流质

normalIntro.en: Build on the family: bounty gives bountiful and its literary twin bounteous.
normalIntro.cn: 从词族入手：bounty 派生出 bountiful 及其书面孪生词 bounteous。

normal.en: bounty comes from Old French bonte, goodness.
normal.cn: bounty 源自古法语 bonte，意为善。

normal.en: -ful turns nouns into adjectives, as in hopeful.
normal.cn: -ful 把名词变成形容词，如 hopeful。

normal.en: a bountiful harvest is literally a harvest full of bounty.
normal.cn: bountiful harvest 字面即「满是善赐的收成」。

normal.en: prize money called a bounty keeps the reward sense alive.
normal.cn: 赏金仍叫 bounty，保留了「奖赏」义。

normal.en: bounteous is the longer, more literary spelling-cousin.
normal.cn: bounteous 是更书面化的近亲拼写。

abstract.en: Picture an urn of plenty that never tips empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一只永远倒不满的丰饶之角。

abstract.en: A generous hand tips the basket toward you without being asked.
abstract.cn: 一只慷慨的手不待你开口就把篮子倾过来。

abstract.en: Goodness that runs over becomes plenty; plenty that runs over becomes generosity.
abstract.cn: 满溢的善成为充足，满溢的充足成为慷慨。

examples.en: A bountiful harvest meant the village could trade grain for salt and cloth.
examples.cn: 丰收使村子可以用谷物换取盐和布匹。

examples.en: The host was bountiful with food, wine, and stories alike.
examples.cn: 主人对食物、美酒和故事都毫不吝惜。

examples.en: Bountiful rains followed the long drought, and the river ran full again.
examples.cn: 久旱之后甘霖丰沛，河水再次涨满。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抱疼副」——抱着满篮果子，抱得胳膊疼还嫌不（副）够多，这就是 bountiful 的丰足画面。

root: 拉丁词根 bon-（好，出自 bonus「好的」）经古法语 bonte（善、慷慨）进入英语作 bounty，再加形容词后缀 -ful 构成。

sensesIntro.en: From sheer abundance the senses move through generous giving and rich yield to fullness of feeling and natural plenty.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项由单纯的数量丰足出发，经慷慨给予与丰饶出产，延伸至情感充盈与自然馈赠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket of goods running over and a hand tipping it toward others
core.cn: 核心意象：满得外溢的篮子，与一只把它倾向他人的手

branches.en: sheer quantity: more than enough, and of many kinds
branches.cn: 纯粹数量：绰绰有余且种类繁多

branches.en: the producer side: fields and orchards that yield richly
branches.cn: 生产者一侧：出产丰厚的田地果园

branches.en: the giver side: free gifts and generous rewards
branches.cn: 给予者一侧：无偿赠予与丰厚奖赏

branches.en: fullness made visible: laughter and laden tables
branches.cn: 可见的充盈：爽朗笑声与满桌盛宴

branches.en: nature's share: plenty no one planted
branches.cn: 自然的一份：无人耕种而成的丰饶

intro.en: The family rests on one Latin root, bon-, with French and English suffixes added step by step.
intro.cn: 该词族建立在拉丁词根 bon- 之上，法语与英语后缀层层叠加。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the root and several living cognates that English knows well.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了词根，也留下若干英语所熟知的同源词。

items.example: bonus is literally a good thing
items.exampleCN: bonus（奖金）字面即「好物」

items.example: bonitas meant goodness in Latin
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 bonitas 意为善

items.example: bonte passed into bounty
items.exampleCN: bonte 演变为英语 bounty

items.example: bountiful is full of bounty
items.exampleCN: bountiful 即「满是慷慨」

items.example: bounteous is the literary twin
items.exampleCN: bounteous 是书面化的孪生词

items.example: benefit is a good done or received
items.exampleCN: benefit（益处）即所做或所受之善

items.example: bountifully means in a bountiful manner
items.exampleCN: bountifully 表示「丰盛地」

items.example: boundary only looks like bounty
items.exampleCN: boundary 与 bounty 只是形近

latinEntries.example: beneficium dare, to grant a favor

definition_zh: 激怒；使恼火；使失去耐心；加剧（书面，指病情或麻烦）
definition_en: to make someone extremely annoyed and frustrated, especially by repeated provocation
core_image: 一块粗糙的石头反复摩擦绳子，把绳子一点点磨起毛
scene: 深夜的会议室里，同一个问题被反复追问，主管终于压不住火气。 After the third round of questions, the same answer began to exasperate the whole team.
sceneCN: 这里 exasperate 是「激怒、使恼火」（第 1 个义项：使人非常生气）；句意：问到第三轮时，同样的回答开始让整个团队恼火。

pos.zh: 激怒；使恼火；使失去耐心

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -tion 构成名词，义为「恼怒；愤懑」
现在分词转形容词，义为「令人恼火的」
过去分词转形容词，义为「被激怒的；又气又无奈的」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「恼火地」

senses.title: To make someone very angry
senses.definition: to make a person extremely annoyed, often so that the anger shows in the voice or face
senses.definitionCN: 使人极为恼火，往往气得在声音或脸色上表露出来
senses.example: Slow traffic and endless forms exasperate most drivers.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢的车流和没完没了的表格让大多数司机恼火。
senses.why: Latin asper means rough, and exasperare meant to make a surface rough; to exasperate a person is to roughen the temper until it turns harsh.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 asper 意为「粗糙」，exasperare 本义是「使表面变粗糙」；激怒一个人，就是把他的脾气磨粗，直到语气变硬。

senses.title: To wear down the patience of someone
senses.titleCN: 使失去耐心；使无可奈何
senses.definition: to exhaust the patience of a person through many small repeated irritations rather than one large offence
senses.definitionCN: 不是一次大的冒犯，而是许多小事反复消耗掉一个人的耐心
senses.example: The endless questions of the child at bedtime exasperated his tired mother.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子临睡前没完没了的问题，让疲惫的母亲失去了耐心。
senses.why: The verb pictures a process rather than a blow, so the object is not struck once but worn thin until patience runs out.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词描绘的是一段过程而不是一次打击，所以对象不是被击中一次，而是被磨薄到耐心耗尽。

senses.title: To be left helplessly annoyed
senses.titleCN: 被弄得又气又无奈（多用被动）
senses.definition: used in the passive, to describe a settled state of frustrated anger with no easy outlet
senses.definitionCN: 多用于被动语态，描述一种找不到出口、已经定型的恼怒与无奈
senses.example: She was exasperated by the refusal of the council to answer her letters.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会始终不回复她的信，她被弄得又气又无奈。
senses.why: In the passive the participle names the end point of the roughening, so the sentence reports a state that has already set in, not an act in progress.
senses.whyCN: 在被动语态里，分词指的是「磨粗」这一过程的结果，所以句子陈述的是一种已经形成的心态，而不是正在进行的动作。

senses.title: To make a bad condition worse
senses.titleCN: 加剧；使（病情、麻烦）恶化（书面，少见）
senses.definition: to intensify an illness, a wound, or a difficulty; a formal and now uncommon use
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、伤口或困难加重；书面语用法，如今已少见
senses.example: Cold winds exasperated the old wound in his leg.
senses.exampleCN: 冷风让他腿上的旧伤更加难熬。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the image: roughening a surface makes a sore place worse, so the same verb once meant to aggravate a disease.
senses.whyCN: 这是意象中最古老的一层：把表面磨粗会让原本疼痛的地方更难受，所以这个动词过去也能表示「使病情加重」。

intro.en: Exasperate comes from Latin exasperare, to make rough, built from ex- and asper, rough; English took the verb in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: exasperate 来自拉丁语 exasperare（使变粗糙），由 ex- 与 asper（粗糙）构成；英语在十六世纪引入这个动词。

items.en: Asper is a Latin adjective meaning rough, harsh, or uneven.
items.cn: asper 是拉丁语形容词，意为粗糙的、严厉的、不平整的。

items.en: Ex- adds the idea of thoroughly or out, and asperare means to make rough.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 加上「彻底、向外」的意思，asperare 意为使变粗糙。

items.en: Exasperare means to roughen and, in transferred use, to provoke or irritate.
items.cn: exasperare 意为使粗糙，引申用法则是挑动、激怒。

items.en: English borrows the verb in the 1500s with the sense of provoking anger.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，义为挑起怒火。

items.en: Later English keeps both the everyday sense of annoying and the older medical sense of worsening a condition.
items.cn: 后来的英语同时保留了「使人恼火」的日常义和「使病情加重」的古老医学义。

note.en: Exasperate belongs to the rough family of asper, and stands at the strong end of the anger words.
note.cn: exasperate 属于 asper（粗糙）这个词族，在表示「生气」的词里处于强烈的一端。

entries.definition: the feeling of being extremely annoyed
entries.definitionCN: 恼怒；愤懑

entries.definition: extremely annoying
entries.definitionCN: 令人恼火的

entries.definition: harshness of manner or tone
entries.definitionCN: （态度或语气的）严厉、粗硬

entries.definition: to make someone slightly angry
entries.definitionCN: 使恼火；使烦躁

entries.definition: to make someone extremely angry
entries.definitionCN: 使大怒

entries.definition: to make someone a little angry
entries.definitionCN: 使烦恼；惹恼

normalIntro.en: Exasperate keeps the Latin word for rough, so the picture is a temper rubbed the wrong way.
normalIntro.cn: exasperate 保留了拉丁语里「粗糙」这个词，所以画面是被逆向摩擦的脾气。

normal.en: Asper in Latin means rough, and exasperate keeps that roughness inside the anger.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 asper 意为粗糙，exasperate 把这份粗糙留在了怒火里。

normal.en: Add the prefix ex- and the verb moves from making rough to making angry.
normal.cn: 加上前缀 ex-，动词就从「使粗糙」走到「使生气」。

normal.en: The noun is exasperation, the worn-out feeling left after repeated annoyance.
normal.cn: 名词是 exasperation，指反复被烦之后留下的那种疲惫的恼怒。

normal.en: Say exasperated by, exasperated at, or exasperated with to name the cause.
normal.cn: 说 exasperated by、exasperated at 或 exasperated with 都能点出原因。

normal.en: Compare irritate: irritate is milder, exasperate is the worn-down stronger end.
normal.cn: 对比 irritate：irritate 较轻，exasperate 是被磨到尽头、更强烈的那一端。

abstract.en: Picture a rough stone dragging across a rope until the fibres stand up.
abstract.cn: 想象一块粗石在绳子上拖过，直到纤维全都竖起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a tap dripping on the same spot all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一个水龙头整夜滴在同一处。

abstract.en: Think of a door that will not open however hard you push.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，无论怎么推都推不开。

examples.en: The constant noise from the building site exasperated the whole street.
examples.cn: 工地不断的噪音让整条街的人都恼火。

examples.en: He was exasperated by the endless delays at the airport.
examples.cn: 机场没完没了的延误把他弄得又气又无奈。

examples.en: Nothing exasperates her more than a meeting with no agenda.
examples.cn: 没有什么比一场没有议程的会议更让她恼火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个在死逼」——被人一步步逼到火气上来，就是被激怒；拆开看是 ex 加 asper（粗糙），粗糙的摩擦让人恼火，这一半才是词源线索，谐音部分只是辅助。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、彻底）+ asper（粗糙）→ exasperare（使粗糙、激怒）→ 拉丁语 exasperatus → 英语 exasperate，核心义「把脾气磨粗糙」。

sensesIntro.en: Exasperate starts as making rough, becomes making angry, then wearing patience thin, then naming a helpless state, and finally worsening a condition.
sensesIntro.cn: exasperate 从「使粗糙」出发，先指使人发火，再指把耐心磨薄，继而指一种无奈的心态，最后指使病情或麻烦加重。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough stone rubbing a rope until it frays.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块粗糙的石头反复摩擦绳子，直到绳子起毛。

branches.en: Roughness turned against a person is the core sense of open anger.
branches.cn: 把粗糙施加到人身上，就是表露在外的怒火这一核心义。

branches.en: Friction repeated many times wears patience down instead of striking once.
branches.cn: 反复的摩擦不是一次打击，而是把耐心一点点磨掉。

branches.en: The passive result is a settled state of helpless anger.
branches.cn: 被动语态的结果，是一种已经定型的无奈怒火。

branches.en: The old medical use keeps the literal idea of making a sore place rougher.
branches.cn: 古老的医学用法保留了「让疼痛处更粗糙」这一字面意思。

branches.en: Both senses share the same picture of a temper being rubbed the wrong way.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同一幅画面：脾气被逆向摩擦。

intro.en: Exasperate is built from the Latin prefix ex- and asper, rough, with English suffixes forming the noun and the two adjectives.
intro.cn: exasperate 由拉丁语前缀 ex- 与 asper（粗糙）构成，英语再用后缀造出名词和两个形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin asper means rough, and exasperare means to make rough and, by transfer, to provoke.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 asper 意为粗糙，exasperare 意为使粗糙，引申为挑动、激怒。

items.example: The prefix ex- strengthens the verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 加强了动词的语气。

items.example: Asper supplies the rough surface.
items.exampleCN: asper 提供粗糙的表面这一意象。

items.example: Asperare turns the adjective into an action.
items.exampleCN: asperare 把这个形容词变成动作。

items.example: Exasperare is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: exasperare 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: Exasperatus gives the passive sense of the result.
items.exampleCN: exasperatus 提供表示结果的被动含义。

items.meaningCN: 由拉丁词干构成动词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ate carries the Latin stem into English.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把拉丁词干带入英语。

items.example: Exasperate keeps the learned tone of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: exasperate 保留了拉丁动词的书面语色彩。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms exasperation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 构成 exasperation。

items.example: Exasperation names the feeling itself.
items.exampleCN: exasperation 指这种情绪本身。

items.meaningCN: 由动词构成形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms exasperating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 exasperating。

definition_zh: 知识产权
definition_en: the legal rights over creations of the mind, such as inventions, texts, designs, marks and secrets
core_image: 一只灯泡里长出一本书与一段旋律，外面罩着一层写着「归创作者」的玻璃罩
scene: 律所把专利、商标与著作权归入同一类案件，统一称为知识产权。 The firm grouped patents, trademarks and copyright under one heading and called them intellectual property.
sceneCN: 这里指「对智力创造成果享有的一组法律权利」，对应第 1 个义项：把发明、文本、标记等无形成果当作财产来保护；句意为律所把专利、商标与著作权归入同一类案件。画面要点：灯泡、书与旋律、玻璃罩。

pos.zh: 知识产权（不可数，作集合名称；指各类具体权利时可作可数用）

derivatives.zh: 智力的；知识分子的（拉丁语中表示「理解」的动词加形容词后缀，指与思考能力有关的）
在智力上（形容词加副词后缀，指从思考能力的角度）
智力；才智（由拉丁语中表示「在…之间挑选」的动词加名词词尾构成，指理解与判断的能力）
智力；情报（同源动词加表性质的名词后缀，语义由「理解」扩展到「理解的结果」与「情报」）

senses.title: Rights over creations of the mind
senses.titleCN: 对智力创造成果的权利总称
senses.definition: the whole family of legal rights that treat inventions, texts, designs and marks as property
senses.definitionCN: 把发明、文本、设计与标记当作财产来保护的一整族法律权利
senses.example: The firm grouped patents, trademarks and copyright under one heading and called them intellectual property.
senses.exampleCN: 律所把专利、商标与著作权归入同一类案件，统称知识产权。
senses.why: The phrase takes the adjective for thinking and joins it to the noun for what is owned, so a product of the mind is treated as a thing that can belong to someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示思考的形容词与表示被拥有之物的名词连在一起，于是心智的产物被当作可以归属某人的东西。

senses.title: Patents over inventions
senses.definition: the exclusive right, granted for a limited term, to make or sell a new invention
senses.definitionCN: 在有限期限内被授予的、制造或销售某项新发明的独占权利
senses.example: A patent is the intellectual property that protects a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 专利是保护一台机器的知识产权。
senses.why: An invention is useful only if it can be worked, so the right is framed as an exclusive power to work it for a set number of years.
senses.whyCN: 发明只有能被实施才有用，因此这项权利被构造成在固定年数内独家实施它的权力。

senses.title: Copyright over texts and music
senses.titleCN: 文本与音乐上的著作权
senses.definition: the right to control copying, performance and adaptation of a written or recorded work
senses.definitionCN: 控制文字或录音作品的复制、表演与改编的权利
senses.example: Copyright protects the melody but not the idea of a song about winter.
senses.exampleCN: 著作权保护那段旋律，却不保护「写一首关于冬天的歌」这个想法。
senses.why: A text can be copied without being taken away, so the right is aimed at copying rather than at possession.
senses.whyCN: 文本可以被复制而并未被夺走，因此这项权利针对的是复制，而不是占有。

senses.title: Trademarks over signs of origin
senses.definition: the right to prevent others from using a sign that identifies the source of goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 阻止他人使用标示商品或服务来源的标记的权利
senses.example: The logo is intellectual property that tells buyers who made the goods.
senses.exampleCN: 这个标识是知识产权，它告诉买方商品由谁制造。
senses.why: A mark has value only because customers rely on it, so the right protects the buyer's recognition as much as the owner's name.
senses.whyCN: 标记之所以有价值，只因为顾客依赖它，因此这项权利既保护所有者的名号，也保护买方的辨识。

senses.title: Trade secrets
senses.definition: protection of confidential information that gives a business an advantage, without publishing it
senses.definitionCN: 对使企业取得优势的保密信息予以保护，而不将其公开
senses.example: The formula is protected as a trade secret rather than as intellectual property registered in an office.
senses.exampleCN: 这个配方作为商业秘密受到保护，而不是作为在主管部门登记的知识产权。
senses.why: Some creations lose their value the moment they are published, so the law protects secrecy instead of granting a public monopoly.
senses.whyCN: 有些创造成果一旦公开就失去价值，因此法律保护的是保密，而不是授予公开的垄断。

senses.title: Industrial designs
senses.definition: the right over the outward appearance of a product, such as its shape, pattern or ornament
senses.definitionCN: 对产品外观（如形状、图案或装饰）享有的权利
senses.example: The shape of the bottle is protected as an industrial design.
senses.exampleCN: 这个瓶子的形状作为外观设计受到保护。
senses.why: Between an invention and a work of art lies a product's look, and the law created a right to cover exactly that middle ground.
senses.whyCN: 在发明与艺术品之间隔着产品的外观，法律创制了一项恰好覆盖这段中间地带的权。

senses.title: The international system
senses.definition: the treaties and offices that let a right obtained in one country be recognised in others
senses.definitionCN: 使在一国取得的权利在别国也获承认的条约与机构
senses.example: A single application can now reach many offices through the international system for intellectual property.
senses.exampleCN: 通过知识产权的国际体系，一份申请现在可以送抵许多主管机构。
senses.why: Ideas cross borders more easily than goods, so the rights over them needed a layer of treaties and common offices.
senses.whyCN: 思想比货物更容易跨越国界，因此对思想的权利需要一层条约与共同的机构。

senses.title: New objects in the digital age
senses.definition: the extension of the same rights to databases, software and algorithms
senses.definitionCN: 把同一组权利扩展到数据库、软件与算法
senses.example: The dispute over the database is a dispute about intellectual property in a new form.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这个数据库的争议，是关于新形态知识产权的争议。
senses.why: Every new medium produces something that can be copied cheaply, and the old family of rights is stretched to cover it.
senses.whyCN: 每一种新媒介都会产生可被廉价复制的东西，于是旧的权利家族被拉长去覆盖它。

intro.en: Intellectual descends from Latin intelligere 'to understand', built on legere 'to choose, gather, read'. Property comes from proprietas 'ownership'. The English phrase was formed in the nineteenth century, when patents and copyright began to be classed together as property.
intro.cn: intellectual 出自拉丁语 intelligere「理解」，建立在 legere「挑选、收集、读」之上。property 出自 proprietas「所有权」。这个英语短语在十九世纪形成，当时专利与著作权开始被归为一类财产。

items.en: Legere meant 'to choose, gather, read'; its sense of picking out explains both reading and the later idea of understanding.
items.cn: legere 意为「挑选、收集、读」；其中「挑出」的意思既解释了阅读，也解释了后来「理解」的观念。

items.en: Intelligere joined the prefix for 'between, among' with legere, literally 'to choose among', and came to mean understanding.
items.cn: intelligere 把表示「在…之间」的前缀与 legere 结合，字面为「在其中挑选」，后来意为理解。

items.en: The adjective intellectualis described what belongs to the understanding rather than to the senses.
items.cn: 形容词 intellectualis 描述属于理解力而非感官的事物。

items.en: Proprietas named ownership, and English property inherited both the legal sense and the sense of a quality.
items.cn: proprietas 指所有权，英语中的 property 继承了它的法律义与「性质」义。

items.en: The phrase was formed in the nineteenth century, when patents, copyright and marks began to be treated as one kind of property. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 这个短语在十九世纪形成，当时专利、著作权与商标开始被当作同一类财产。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for choosing and reading but has split into understanding, clarity and a social type; the second group gives the neighbouring legal categories.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「挑选与阅读」的拉丁动词，但已分成理解、清晰与一种社会身份；第二组是相邻的法律类别。

entries.definition: The power of understanding and reasoning; it names the capacity, not the rights over what the capacity produces.
entries.definitionCN: 理解与推理的能力；它命名能力本身，而不是对能力产物所享的权利。

entries.definition: Able to learn and reason well; it describes a person or device rather than a legal category.
entries.definitionCN: 善于学习与推理的；它描述人或设备，而不是一个法律类别。

entries.definition: Capable of being understood; it concerns how clear something is, not who owns it.
entries.definitionCN: 可被理解的；它关心某物有多清楚，而不是归谁所有。

entries.definition: The view that reason is the chief source of knowledge; it is a philosophical position, not a property right.
entries.definitionCN: 认为理性是知识主要来源的主张；它是一种哲学立场，不是财产权。

entries.definition: A non-physical item of value on a balance sheet; it is wider and includes goodwill and brands that may not be protected rights.
entries.definitionCN: 资产负债表中不具实体的有价值项目；它范围更宽，包括未必受权利保护的商誉与品牌。

entries.definition: The older name for patents, marks and designs, as opposed to literary and artistic works.
entries.definitionCN: 专利、商标与外观设计较早的称法，与文学艺术作品相对。

entries.definition: The specific right over copying and performance of a work; it is one part of the entry phrase, not its whole.
entries.definitionCN: 对作品复制与表演的具体权利；它是本短语的一部分，而不是全部。

entries.definition: An exclusive right granted for an invention; like copyright it is one branch of the wider family.
entries.definitionCN: 为一项发明授予的独占权利；与著作权一样，它只是更大家族中的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verbs for choosing and understanding, the noun for ownership, real derived words and real legal categories.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「挑选」与「理解」的动词、表示所有权的名词、真实派生词与真实法律类别。

normal.en: The first word points to the mind, the second to ownership, so the phrase means owning what the mind makes.
normal.cn: 前一个词指向心智，后一个词指向所有，因此这个短语意为拥有心智所造之物。

normal.en: The family runs intellect, intellectual, intellectually and intelligence.
normal.cn: 同族词包括智力、智力的、在智力上，以及由同一词根发展出的「情报」一词。

normal.en: The field has four common members: patent, copyright, trademark and trade secret.
normal.cn: 这个领域有四个常见成员：专利、著作权、商标与商业秘密。

normal.en: A song can be protected even though nothing physical is held, which is why the phrase speaks of property in an idea.
normal.cn: 一首歌可以在没有任何实体持有时受到保护，所以这个短语说的是对想法的财产。

normal.en: Registration offices and treaties exist because ideas cross borders more easily than goods.
normal.cn: 登记机构与条约之所以存在，是因为思想比货物更容易跨越国界。

abstract.en: Picture a glass dome over a light bulb, a book and a scrap of melody, with a name written on the dome.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃罩罩住灯泡、书与一小段旋律，罩上写着一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens only the copy of a text and never the original.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙只能打开文本的复制件，却永远打不开原件。

abstract.en: Picture a locked drawer inside a factory that holds a formula no one is allowed to see.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂里一只上锁的抽屉，里面放着不许任何人查看的配方。

examples.en: The treaty raised the level of protection for intellectual property.
examples.cn: 该条约提高了知识产权的保护水平。

examples.en: Small firms often fail to register their intellectual property in time.
examples.cn: 小企业常常未能及时登记自己的知识产权。

examples.en: The case turned on whether a database counts as intellectual property.
examples.cn: 该案的争点在于数据库是否算作知识产权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「脑袋里的家产」——先想「智力」，再想「财产」：凡是脑子造出来、又能被复制的，都可以像房产一样登记归属。

root: intellectual 出自拉丁语 intelligere「理解」，由表示「在…之间」的前缀与 legere「挑选、读」构成；property 出自 proprietas「所有权」，源头为 proprius「自己的」，其更深来源不确定。整个短语是十九世纪形成的法律复合名称。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings fan out from one idea: the mind's product treated as property. The general family comes first; then patents, copyright, marks, secrets and designs, each protecting a different kind of creation; then the international layer that carries the rights across borders; and finally the new objects of the digital age.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个观念展开：把心智的产物当作财产。先是整个家族；其次是专利、著作权、商标、商业秘密与外观设计，各自保护不同种类的创造；再其次是让权利跨越国界的国际层面；最后是数字时代的新对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a creation of the mind enclosed in a dome bearing the maker's name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件心智创造被罩在写有创作者名字的玻璃罩里。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the general name for rights over creations of the mind.
branches.cn: 家族：对智力创造成果所享权利的总称。

branches.en: INVENTION AND DESIGN: a working machine, and the outward look of a product.
branches.cn: 发明与设计：一台能运转的机器，以及一个产品的外表。

branches.en: TEXT AND MELODY: the right aimed at copying rather than at possession.
branches.cn: 文本与旋律：针对复制而非占有的权利。

branches.en: MARKS AND SECRETS: signs that identify a source, and information kept out of sight.
branches.cn: 标记与秘密：标示来源的符号，以及被藏在视线之外的信息。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND NEW FORMS: treaties that cross borders, and databases and software that stretch the old family.
branches.cn: 保护与新形态：跨越国界的条约，以及拉长旧家族边界的数据库与软件。

intro.en: Two Latin strands meet: a verb for choosing and reading, which gives the whole intellect family, and an adjective for 'one's own', which gives property and its relatives.
intro.cn: 两条拉丁语线索在此相遇：一个表示「挑选与阅读」的动词给出整个智力词族，一个表示「自己的」形容词给出「财产」及其亲属词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the verb of understanding, its noun and adjective, and the noun for ownership.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了表示理解的动词、它的名词与形容词，以及表示所有权的名词。

definition_zh: 痛斥；严责；训斥；大骂
definition_en: to scold or criticize someone angrily and at length
core_image: 指着鼻子、唾沫横飞的长篇怒斥
scene: 经理当着全办公室的面指着报表高声数落。 The manager berated the intern for the tiny accounting error.
sceneCN: 这里 berated 是「痛斥、严责」（第 1 个义项：愤怒地长时间责骂）；句意是经理当众为一个小的账目错误痛斥实习生。

derivatives.zh: 基础词的古义「申斥」，今义「评级」
由现在分词转名词，义为「痛斥；一顿臭骂」

senses.title: To scold angrily and at length
senses.definition: to speak to someone angrily for a long time about their fault
senses.definitionCN: 因对方的过错愤怒地长时间责骂
senses.example: The manager berated the intern for the tiny accounting error.
senses.exampleCN: 经理为一个小的账目错误痛斥实习生。
senses.why: Be- strengthens rate, an old word for scold, so it is scolding hard.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 be- 强化古义「申斥」的 rate，即狠狠地骂。

senses.title: To blame oneself bitterly
senses.definition: to scold oneself inwardly for a fault or failure
senses.definitionCN: 在心里为自己的过错或失败狠狠责备自己
senses.example: She berated herself all night for the missed deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 她为错过的截止日期自责了一整夜。
senses.why: The scolding turns inward onto oneself.
senses.whyCN: 「痛斥」的对象转向自身，成为自责。

intro.en: Berate is the prefix be- plus rate, an older English verb meaning to scold.
intro.cn: berate 由前缀 be- 加 rate 构成，rate 在旧义中指「申斥」。

items.en: reta meant to scold, to find fault.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 reta 意为「责骂、挑错」。

items.en: raten meant to chide or scold.
items.cn: 中古英语 raten 意为「斥责」。

items.en: the compound berate appeared in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 复合词 berate 出现于十六世纪。

items.en: it settled into use for angry, lengthy scolding.
items.cn: 十七、十八世纪固定用于愤怒的长篇责骂。

items.en: the plain verb rate lost the scolding sense, but berate keeps it.
items.cn: 动词 rate 单独使用已失去申斥义，该义只存于 berate。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the be- prefix or spelling; the near-meaning group gathers scolding words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 be- 前缀或拼写；近义组汇集责骂类词。
